title.zh: 卷二百六十九 列傳第二十八 陶穀 扈蒙 王著 王祐 楊昭儉 魚崇諒 張澹 高錫
title.en: Volume 269 Biographies 28: Tao Gu, Hu Meng, Wang Zhe, Wang You, Yang Zhaojian, Yu Chongliang, Zhang Dan, Gao Xi
title.raw: 卷二百六十九 列傳第二十八 陶穀 扈蒙 王著 王祐 楊昭儉 魚崇諒 張澹 高錫 Volume 269 Biographies 28: Tao Gu, Hu Meng, Wang Zhe, Wang You, Yang Zhaojian, Yu Chongliang, Zhang Dan, Gao Xi

sentences.zh: 陶穀，字秀實，邠州新平人。

translations.literal: Tao Gu, courtesy name Xiushi, was a native of Xinping in Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Gu, styled Xiushi, came from Xinping in Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 本姓唐，避晉祖諱改焉。

translations.literal: His original surname was Tang; he changed it to avoid the taboo name of the Jin founding emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The family had originally borne the surname Tang but changed it to evade the imperial taboo of the Jin founder.

sentences.zh: 歷北齊、隋、唐為名族。

translations.literal: Through Northern Qi, Sui, and Tang they were a distinguished clan.
translations.idiomatic: For generations under the Northern Qi, Sui, and Tang they had ranked among the great families.

sentences.zh: 祖彥謙，歷慈、絳、澧三州刺史，有詩名，自號鹿門先生。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yanqian served as prefect of Ci, Jiang, and Li prefectures, had a reputation in poetry, and styled himself Master of Deer Gate.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yanqian had served as prefect of Ci, Jiang, and Li, won renown as a poet, and took the sobriquet Master of Deer Gate.

sentences.zh: 父渙，領夷州刺史，唐季之亂，為邠帥楊崇本所害。

translations.literal: His father Huan held the post of prefect of Yi Prefecture; in the turmoil at the end of Tang he was killed by the Bin military commissioner Yang Chongben.
translations.idiomatic: His father Huan had governed Yi Prefecture, but during the chaos at the close of the Tang he was slain by Yang Chongben, the military governor of Bin.

sentences.zh: 時穀尚幼，隨母柳氏育崇本家。

translations.literal: At that time Gu was still young; he followed his mother the Lady Liu and was raised in Chongben's household.
translations.idiomatic: Gu was still a child then and grew up in Chongben's house with his mother, Lady Liu.

sentences.zh: 十餘歲，能屬文，起家校書郎、單州軍事判官。

translations.literal: By his mid-teens he could compose essays; he began his career as a proofreader and as military adjutant in Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before he was twenty he could already write essays, and he entered service as a collator in the palace library and as adjutant on the Shanzhou military staff.

sentences.zh: 嘗以書干宰相李崧，崧甚重其文。

translations.literal: He once presented a letter to the chief minister Li Song, and Song greatly valued his writing.
translations.idiomatic: He once submitted a literary work to Chief Minister Li Song, who thought very highly of his prose.

sentences.zh: 時和凝亦為相，同奏為著作佐郎、集賢校理。

translations.literal: At that time He Ning was also a chief minister; together they memorialized to appoint him Associate Editor in the Secretariat and collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He Ning was serving as chief minister at the same time, and the two of them jointly recommended him for posts as associate editor in the Secretariat and collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 改監察御史，分司西京，遷虞部員外郎、知制誥。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Investigating Censor, detached to the Western Capital, and promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Works and drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made an investigating censor assigned to the western capital, and later promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Works with responsibility for drafting imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 會晉祖廢翰林學士，兼掌內外制。

translations.literal: When the Jin founding emperor abolished the Hanlin Academy, Gu took charge of both internal and external edicts.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin founder abolished the Hanlin Academy, Gu assumed responsibility for drafting both palace and court proclamations.

sentences.zh: 詞目繁委，穀言多委愜，為當時最。

translations.literal: The drafting tasks were numerous and complex; many were delegated to Gu and handled to satisfaction, and his drafts were rated the foremost of the time.
translations.idiomatic: With the volume of edicts overwhelming, much of the work was entrusted to Gu and carried out to general satisfaction, and his drafts were regarded as the best of the age.

sentences.zh: 少帝初，賜緋袍、靴、笏、黑銀帶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shaodi reign he was granted a crimson robe, boots, court tablet, and black silver belt.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the reign of Emperor Shaodi he received the crimson robe, boots, court tablet, and black silver belt.

sentences.zh: 天福九年，加倉部郎中。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Tianfu he was promoted to Director of the Ministry of Revenues.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of the Tianfu era he was made director in the Ministry of Revenues.

sentences.zh: 初，崧從契丹以北，高祖入京師，以崧第賜蘇逢吉，而崧別有田宅在西京，逢吉皆取之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Song followed the Khitans northward, Gaozu entered the capital and granted Song's residence to Su Fengji; Song also had separate fields and houses in the Western Capital, and Fengji took them all.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Li Song had gone north with the Khitans, Gaozu entered the capital and gave Song's mansion to Su Fengji; Song still owned other estates in the western capital, and Fengji seized those as well.

sentences.zh: 崧自北還，因以宅券獻逢吉，逢吉不悅，而崧子弟數出怨言。

translations.literal: When Song returned from the north he therefore presented the deed of the house to Fengji; Fengji was displeased, and Song's sons and younger relatives repeatedly uttered complaints.
translations.idiomatic: When Song came back from the north he offered the deed of the house to Fengji, but Fengji was not appeased, and Song's sons and nephews kept voicing grievances.

sentences.zh: 其後逢吉乃誘告崧與弟嶼、嶬等下獄，崧懼，移病不出。

translations.literal: Thereafter Fengji induced accusations that Song and his brothers Yu and Wei and others be imprisoned; Song was afraid and pleaded illness and did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji then engineered charges that sent Song and his brothers Yu and Wei to prison; in fear Song pleaded illness and refused to leave his home.

sentences.zh: 崧族子昉為秘書郎，嘗往候崧，崧語昉曰：「邇來朝廷於我有何議？

translations.literal: Song's clansman Fang was a secretary; he once went to visit Song, and Song said to Fang, "Of late has the court had any discussion concerning me?
translations.idiomatic: Song's kinsman Fang, who served as a secretary in the palace archives, once called on him, and Song asked Fang, "Has the court been saying anything about me lately?

sentences.zh: 」昉曰：「無他聞，唯陶給事往往於稠人中厚誣叔父。

translations.literal: " Fang said, "I have heard nothing else, only that Drafting Attendant Tao often slanders my uncle severely in crowded gatherings.
translations.idiomatic: " Fang replied, "Nothing else that I know of—only that Drafting Attendant Tao keeps spreading harsh slanders against you in public gatherings.

sentences.zh: 」崧歎曰：「穀自單州判官，吾取為集賢校理，不數年擢掌誥命，吾何負於陶氏子哉？

translations.literal: " Song sighed and said, "Gu began as adjutant in Shan Prefecture; I took him as collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and within a few years he was promoted to handle edicts—what have I done to wrong the son of the Tao family?
translations.idiomatic: " Song sighed and said, "When Gu was only a Shanzhou adjutant I brought him into the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and within a few years I had him drafting edicts—what debt does that Tao boy think I owe him?

sentences.zh: 」及崧遇禍，昉嘗因公事詣穀，穀問昉：「識李侍中否？

translations.literal: " When Song met disaster, Fang once went to Gu on official business; Gu asked Fang, "Do you know Vice Minister Li?
translations.idiomatic: " After Song fell victim to the purge, Fang once called on Gu on official business, and Gu asked him, "Do you know Vice Minister Li?

sentences.zh: 」昉斂衽應曰：「遠從叔爾。

translations.literal: " Fang straightened his robe and replied, "He is my distant uncle.
translations.idiomatic: " Fang straightened his garments and answered, "He is my father's cousin.

sentences.zh: 」穀曰：「李氏之禍，穀出力焉。

translations.literal: " Gu said, "In the disaster of the Li family, Gu exerted effort for it.
translations.idiomatic: " Gu said, "I had a hand in bringing down the Li family.

sentences.zh: 」昉聞之汗出。

translations.literal: " When Fang heard this he broke into a sweat.
translations.idiomatic: " Fang broke out in a cold sweat at the words.

sentences.zh: 穀性急率，嘗與兗帥安審信集會，杯酒相失，為審信所奏。

translations.literal: Gu's nature was impetuous and direct; he once attended a gathering with the Yan military commissioner An Shenxin, and over wine they fell out, and Shenxin memorialized against him.
translations.idiomatic: Gu was brusque by temperament; at a banquet with Yanzhou commander An Shenxin he quarreled over wine, and Shenxin reported him to the throne.

sentences.zh: 時方姑息武臣，穀坐責授太常少卿。

translations.literal: At that time military officers were being indulged; Gu was punished by appointment as Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then indulging its military commanders, and Gu was demoted to vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 嘗上言：「頃蒞西臺，每見臺司詳斷刑獄，少有即時決者。

translations.literal: He once submitted a memorial saying, "When I recently served at the Western Capital, I often saw the capital office review and decide criminal cases, and few were decided on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: He once memorialized, "During my recent service at the western capital I found that the capital judicial office rarely rendered immediate decisions in criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 至於閭閻夫婦小有爭訟，淹滯積時，坊市死亡喪葬，必俟臺司判狀，奴婢病亡，亦須檢驗。

translations.literal: As for minor disputes between husbands and wives in the lanes, they dragged on for long periods; deaths and burials in the wards and markets had to await the capital office's written judgment, and when male or female servants died of illness they also had to be examined.
translations.idiomatic: Even petty quarrels between neighbors were left to fester for months; burials in the wards could not proceed until the capital office issued its ruling, and when a servant died of illness an official inspection was still required.

sentences.zh: 吏因緣為姦，而邀求不已，經旬不獲埋瘞。

translations.literal: Clerks used the opportunity to commit wrongdoing and made unending demands; for ten days or more burial was not obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks exploited the delays to extort bribes, and corpses sometimes lay unburied for ten days or more.

sentences.zh: 望申條約以革其弊。

translations.literal: I hope regulations may be promulgated to reform these abuses.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that clear regulations be issued to eliminate these abuses.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The court approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 俄拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was appointed Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made a drafter in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 嘗請教習樂工、停二舞郎，及禁民伐桑棗為薪，並從其請。

translations.literal: He once requested instruction for music workers, abolition of the two dance attendants, and prohibition of the people cutting mulberry and jujube for firewood; all his requests were granted.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that palace musicians receive proper training, that two dance attendants be abolished, and that commoners be forbidden to cut mulberry and jujube trees for fuel—all of which were approved.

sentences.zh: 開運三年，賜金紫。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaiyun he was granted gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Kaiyun era he received the gold-and-purple insignia of high rank.

sentences.zh: 契丹主北歸，脅穀令從行。

translations.literal: When the Khitan ruler returned north, he coerced Gu to accompany him on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan emperor withdrew northward he tried to force Gu to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 穀逃匿僧舍中，衣布褐，陽為行者狀。

translations.literal: Gu fled and hid in a monks' quarters, wore coarse cloth, and pretended to be a traveler.
translations.idiomatic: Gu hid in a monastery, dressed in plain hemp cloth, and passed himself off as a wandering monk.

sentences.zh: 軍士意其詐，持刃陵脅者日數四。

translations.literal: Soldiers suspected he was deceiving them; those who held blades and intimidated him came four times a day.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers suspected the disguise, and as many as four times a day armed men threatened him at knifepoint.

sentences.zh: 穀頗工歷數，謂同輩曰：「西南五星連珠，漢地當有王者出。

translations.literal: Gu was quite skilled in calendrical astronomy and said to his companions, "In the southwest the five stars are strung like pearls; in the Han lands a king ought to arise.
translations.idiomatic: Gu was well versed in astronomy and told his companions, "The five planets are aligned in the southwest—a king will rise in the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 契丹主必不得歸國。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler will certainly not be able to return to his state.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler will never make it home alive.

sentences.zh: 」及耶律德光死，有孛光芒指北，穀曰：「自此契丹自相魚肉，永不亂華矣。

translations.literal: " When Yelü Deguang died, a broom star's light pointed north; Gu said, "From this time the Khitans will devour one another and never again disturb the Huaxia lands.
translations.idiomatic: " When Yelü Deguang died and a comet's tail pointed north, Gu said, "From now on the Khitans will tear one another apart and never again trouble China.

sentences.zh: 」遂歸漢，為給事中。

translations.literal: " He then returned to the Han and served as Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: " He then made his way back to the Later Han court and was appointed supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 乾祐中，令常參官轉對。

translations.literal: During the Qianyou era regular-attendance officials were ordered to take turns presenting memorials at court.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianyou reign the court ordered officials in regular attendance to take turns addressing the throne.

sentences.zh: 穀上言曰：「五日上章，曾非舊制。

translations.literal: Gu submitted a memorial saying, "Presenting memorials every five days was never an old institution.
translations.idiomatic: Gu memorialized, "The rule of submitting memorials every five days was never part of the old system.

sentences.zh: 百官敘對，且異昌言。

translations.literal: For all officials to speak in turn moreover differs from beneficial words.
translations.idiomatic: Having every official speak in rotation is hardly the same as offering sound counsel.

sentences.zh: 徒浼天聰，無益時政，欲乞停轉對。

translations.literal: It merely defiles the imperial ear and benefits current administration not at all; I wish to request cessation of the rotation.
translations.idiomatic: It only burdens Your Majesty's attention without helping governance, and I ask that the rotation be discontinued.

sentences.zh: 在朝群臣有所聞見，即許不時詣闕聞奏。

translations.literal: When officials at court have something they have heard or seen, let them be permitted to come to the palace gate at irregular times to report and memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a court official learns something worth reporting, let him be allowed to come to the palace at any time to inform the throne.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 世宗嚐謂宰相曰：「朕觀歷代君臣治平之道，誠為不易。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong once said to the chief ministers, "I observe that the way of rulers and ministers through the ages in bringing order and peace is truly not easy.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong once told his chief ministers, "Looking at how rulers and ministers of past ages achieved peace and good government, I see that it is no easy thing.

sentences.zh: 又念唐、晉失德之後，亂臣黠將，僭竊者多。

translations.literal: I also reflect that after Tang and Jin lost virtue, rebellious ministers and cunning generals who usurped were many.
translations.idiomatic: I also recall that after the Tang and Jin courts lost their moral authority, treacherous ministers and cunning generals seized power again and again.

sentences.zh: 今中原甫定，吳、蜀、幽、并尚未平附，聲教未能遠被，宜令近臣各為論策，宣導經濟之略。

translations.literal: Now the Central Plains have just been settled; Wu, Shu, You, and Bing are not yet pacified and attached; imperial influence has not yet reached far—it is fitting to order close ministers each to compose policy essays expounding strategies of statecraft.
translations.idiomatic: The central plains have only just been secured, while Wu, Shu, You, and Bing still stand outside our rule and our civilizing influence has not yet spread far. I should have my close advisers each draft policy essays setting out plans for governing the realm.

sentences.zh: 」乃命承旨徐台符以下二十餘人，各撰《為君難為臣不易論》、《平邊策》以進。

translations.literal: " He then ordered Academician-in-Chief Xu Taifu and more than twenty others each to compose "On the Difficulty of Being Ruler and the Hardship of Being Minister" and "Strategies for Pacifying the Borders" and present them.
translations.idiomatic: " He then ordered Chief Academician Xu Taifu and more than twenty others to write treatises titled On the Difficulties of Rulership and Ministerial Service and Strategies for Pacifying the Frontiers and submit them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 其策率以修文德、來遠人為意，惟穀與竇儀、楊昭儉、王樸以封疆密邇江、淮，當用師取之。

translations.literal: Their strategies mostly took cultivating civil virtue and drawing distant people as their intent; only Gu, Dou Yi, Yang Zhaojian, and Wang Pu held that because the borders lay close to the Yangzi and Huai, troops ought to be used to take them.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the essays urged cultivating civil virtue and winning over distant peoples, but Gu, Dou Yi, Yang Zhaojian, and Wang Pu argued that because our borders lay hard against the Yangzi and Huai regions, military force should be used to seize them.

sentences.zh: 世宗自克高平，常訓兵講武，思混一天下。

translations.literal: Since Shizong conquered Gaoping he had constantly trained troops and discussed military affairs, thinking to unite all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since his victory at Gaoping, Shizong had drilled his armies and studied strategy with an eye to reunifying the empire.

sentences.zh: 及覽其策，忻然聽納，由是平南之意益堅矣。

translations.literal: When he read their strategies he gladly listened and adopted them; thereby his intent to pacify the south grew firmer.
translations.idiomatic: When he read these essays he welcomed their counsel, and his determination to conquer the south grew all the stronger.

sentences.zh: 顯德三年，遷兵部侍郎，加承旨。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiande he was transferred to Vice Minister of War and added as Academician-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiande he was promoted to vice minister of war and made chief academician of the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 世宗留心稼穡，命工刻木為耕夫、織婦、蠶女之狀，置於禁中，思廣勸課之道，穀為讚辭以進。

translations.literal: Shizong attended to agriculture; he ordered craftsmen to carve wood into forms of plowman, weaving woman, and silkworm girl and place them in the inner palace, thinking to extend the way of encouraging farming; Gu composed laudatory inscriptions and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong took a close interest in agriculture and had artisans carve wooden figures of a plowman, a weaver, and a silkworm keeper for display in the inner palace as a way to promote farming; Gu wrote laudatory inscriptions and presented them.

sentences.zh: 顯德六年，加吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xiande he was added as Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Xiande he was also made vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 宋初，轉禮部尚書，依前翰林承旨。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was transferred to Minister of Rites while continuing as before as Hanlin Academician-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he was made minister of rites while retaining his post as chief Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 穀在翰林，與竇儀不協，儀有公望，慮其軋己，嘗附宰相趙普與趙逄、高錫輩共排儀，儀終不至相位。

translations.literal: When Gu was in the Hanlin he was not on good terms with Dou Yi; Yi had public esteem, and Gu feared Yi would crowd him out; he once attached himself to Chief Minister Zhao Pu and Zhao Feng, Gao Xi, and others jointly to exclude Yi, and Yi in the end never reached the chief ministership.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in the Hanlin, Gu clashed with Dou Yi, whose public standing he feared would eclipse his own; he joined Chief Minister Zhao Pu, Zhao Feng, Gao Xi, and others in a campaign to block Yi, and Yi never rose to chief minister.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年，判吏部銓兼知貢舉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiande he adjudicated the Ministry of Personnel selection and concurrently supervised the civil service examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qiande he oversaw personnel selection in the Ministry of Personnel and supervised the civil service examinations.

sentences.zh: 再為南郊禮儀使，法物制度，多穀所定。

translations.literal: He again served as commissioner for suburban rites; ritual implements and regulations were largely set by Gu.
translations.idiomatic: He again directed the southern suburban sacrifices, and most of the ritual regalia and procedures were established by him.

sentences.zh: 時范質為大禮使，以鹵簿清遊隊有甲騎具裝，莫知其制度，以問於穀。

translations.literal: At that time Fan Zhi was grand ritual commissioner; in the imperial guard's pure excursion formation there were armored cavalry in full equipment, and no one knew their regulations, so he asked Gu.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhi was then serving as grand ritual commissioner and, finding that the imperial procession's escort included armored cavalry in full trappings whose specifications were unknown, asked Gu about them.

sentences.zh: 穀曰：「梁貞明丁丑歲，河南尹張全義獻人甲三百副、馬具裝二百副。

translations.literal: Gu said, "In the dingchou year of Zhenming of Liang, Henan governor Zhang Quanyi presented three hundred sets of infantry armor and two hundred sets of horse equipment.
translations.idiomatic: Gu replied, "In the dingchou year of Liang's Zhenming reign, Zhang Quanyi, governor of Henan, presented three hundred sets of infantry armor and two hundred sets of horse trappings.

sentences.zh: 其人甲以布為裏，黃絁表之，青綠畫為甲文，紅錦綠青絁為下帬，絳韋為絡，金銅玦，長短至膝。

translations.literal: The infantry armor used cloth as lining, yellow ge as outer layer, blue-green painted as armor pattern, red brocade and green-blue ge as lower skirt, crimson leather as lacing, gold and bronze rings, length reaching to the knee.
translations.idiomatic: The infantry armor was lined with cloth, faced with yellow ge, painted in blue-green to resemble lamellar plates, with skirts of red brocade and green-blue ge, laced with crimson leather and fitted with gold and bronze fittings, reaching to the knee.

sentences.zh: 前膺為人面二目，背連膺纏以紅錦騰蛇。

translations.literal: The breastplate bore a human face with two eyes; the back connecting to the breast was wound with red brocade in the form of a soaring serpent.
translations.idiomatic: The breastplate bore a human face with two eyes, and the back piece was joined to it with red brocade worked in the pattern of a soaring serpent.

sentences.zh: 馬具裝蓋尋常馬甲，但加珂拂於前膺及後鞦爾。

translations.literal: Horse equipment was essentially ordinary horse armor, only with ornamental plumes added to the fore-breast and rear crupper.
translations.idiomatic: The horse trappings were essentially ordinary horse armor, with ornamental plumes added only to the chest piece and the crupper.

sentences.zh: 莊宗入洛，悉焚毀。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong entered Luoyang, all were burned and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong entered Luoyang, the whole stock was burned.

sentences.zh: 」質命有司如穀說，造以給用。

translations.literal: " Zhi ordered the relevant offices to follow Gu's account and manufacture them for use.
translations.idiomatic: " Fan Zhi ordered the appropriate offices to follow Gu's specifications and manufacture replacements.

sentences.zh: 又乘輿大輦，久亡其制，穀創意造之，後承用焉。

translations.literal: Also the great imperial carriage had long lost its specifications; Gu devised and created it, and later generations continued to use it.
translations.idiomatic: The great imperial carriage had also long since lost its specifications; Gu designed a new one that remained in use thereafter.

sentences.zh: 明德門成，詔穀為之記。

translations.literal: When the Gate of Illustrious Virtue was completed, the emperor ordered Gu to compose its inscription.
translations.idiomatic: When the Gate of Illustrious Virtue was completed, the court commissioned Gu to write its commemorative inscription.

sentences.zh: 乾德中，命庫部員外郎王貽孫、《周易》博士奚嶼同考試品官子弟。

translations.literal: During Qiande he ordered Vice Director of the Treasury Bureau Wang Yisun and Doctor of the Book of Changes Xi Yu jointly to examine sons of officials of rank.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qiande era he appointed Vice Director Wang Yisun of the treasury bureau and Doctor of the Changes Xi Yu to examine the sons of ranked officials.

sentences.zh: 穀屬其子鄑於嶼，鄑書不通，以合格聞，補殿中省進馬。

translations.literal: Gu entrusted his son Zou to Yu; Zou's writing was not proficient, yet he was reported as qualified and appointed horse-presenter in the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: Gu asked Xi Yu to look after his son Zou, whose examination papers were incompetent yet were reported as passing, and Zou was appointed presenter of horses in the palace domestic service.

sentences.zh: 俄為人所發，下御史府案問，嶼責授乾州司戶，貽孫責授左贊善大夫，奪穀奉兩月。

translations.literal: Shortly it was exposed by someone; the case was sent down to the Censorate for investigation; Yu was punished by appointment as revenue clerk in Qian Prefecture, Yisun punished by appointment as Left Supporter of the Heir Apparent, and Gu's salary was withheld for two months.
translations.idiomatic: The affair was soon exposed; the censorate investigated; Xi Yu was demoted to revenue clerk in Qianzhou, Wang Yisun to left supporter of the heir apparent, and Gu's salary was suspended for two months.

sentences.zh: 穀後累加刑部、戶部二尚書。

translations.literal: Later Gu was repeatedly promoted to the two ministries of Punishments and Revenue as minister.
translations.idiomatic: Gu was later promoted in succession to minister of punishments and minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 開寶三年，卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaibao he died, aged sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Kaibao at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈右僕射。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 穀強記嗜學，博通經史，諸子佛老，咸所總覽；

translations.literal: Gu had a powerful memory and loved learning; he was broadly versed in the classics and histories, and the masters, Buddhism, and Daoism—he surveyed them all;
translations.idiomatic: Gu had an extraordinary memory and loved learning; he mastered the classics and histories and had read widely in the philosophical masters, Buddhist texts, and Daoist writings;

sentences.zh: 多蓄法書名畫，善隸書。

translations.literal: he stored many model calligraphies and famous paintings and was skilled in clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: he collected many fine calligraphies and famous paintings and wrote an excellent clerical hand.

sentences.zh: 為人雋辨宏博，然奔競務進，見後學有文采者，必極言以譽之；

translations.literal: As a man he was sharp in debate and vast in learning, yet he rushed and competed for advancement; when he saw younger scholars with literary talent he always spoke to the utmost to praise them;
translations.idiomatic: He was sharp-witted and learned, but ambitious and eager to advance; whenever he met a talented junior scholar he lavished praise on him;

sentences.zh: 聞達官有聞望者，則巧詆以排之，其多忌好名類此。

translations.literal: when he heard that a high official had reputation and esteem, he would craftily slander to exclude him—his jealousy and love of fame were mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: yet when he heard of a senior official with a strong reputation, he would contrive slanders to bring him down—his jealousy and hunger for fame showed in countless ways like this.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖將受禪，未有禪文，穀在旁，出諸懷中而進之曰：「已成矣。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Taizu was about to receive the abdication, there was not yet an abdication document; Gu was at his side, took it from his bosom and presented it saying, "It is already finished.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu was preparing to accept the abdication, no abdication text had yet been drafted; Gu stood beside him, pulled a document from his robe, and presented it with the words, "It is already done.

sentences.zh: 」太祖甚薄之。

translations.literal: " Taizu thought very little of this.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizu despised him for it.

sentences.zh: 嘗自曰：「吾頭骨法相非常，當戴貂蟬冠爾。

translations.literal: He once said of himself, "The physiognomy of my skull is extraordinary; I ought to wear the cicada-bedecked hat.
translations.idiomatic: He once said of himself, "The bone structure of my skull is extraordinary—I am destined to wear the premier's cap with its cicada ornament.

sentences.zh: 」蓋有意大用也，人多笑之。

translations.literal: " He plainly intended great employment, and many people laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: " He clearly meant that he was destined for the highest office, and many people mocked him for it.

sentences.zh: 子邴，至起居舍人。

translations.literal: His son Bing rose to Attendant of the Imperial Diary.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bing rose to the post of attendant of the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 天禧四年，錄穀孫寔試秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianxi, Gu's grandson Shi was recorded and tested as collator in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianxi, Gu's grandson Shi passed the examination for collator in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 扈蒙，字日用，幽州安次人。

translations.literal: Hu Meng, courtesy name Riyong, was a native of Anci in You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Meng, styled Riyong, came from Anci in You Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 曾祖洋，涿州別駕。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yang was vice prefect of Zhuo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yang had served as vice prefect of Zhuo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖智周，盧龍軍節度推官。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhizhou was judicial aide to the Luolong military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhizhou had been a judicial aide on the staff of the Luolong military governor.

sentences.zh: 父曾，內園使。

translations.literal: His father Zeng was commissioner of the inner gardens.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zeng had been commissioner of the imperial gardens.

sentences.zh: 蒙少能文，晉天福中，舉進士，入漢為鄠縣主簿。

translations.literal: Meng from youth could write; in the Tianfu era of Jin he passed the jinshi examination and entered Han service as registrar of E County.
translations.idiomatic: Meng showed literary talent early; during the Jin Tianfu era he passed the jinshi examination, and under the Later Han he served as registrar of E County.

sentences.zh: 趙思綰叛，遣郭從義討之。

translations.literal: When Zhao Sizong rebelled, Guo Congyi was dispatched to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Sizong rebelled, Guo Congyi was sent to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 郡縣吏供給皆戎服趨事，蒙冠服褒博，舉止舒緩，從義頗訝之。

translations.literal: County and prefecture clerks in supplying all wore military dress and hurried in service; Meng wore cap and robes broad and ample, his bearing leisurely and slow, and Congyi was quite astonished.
translations.idiomatic: The county and prefectural officials all wore military dress as they hurried about their duties, but Meng appeared in full scholarly robes and moved with unhurried grace, which greatly surprised Congyi.

sentences.zh: 轉運使李穀謂曰：「蒙文學名流，不習吏事。

translations.literal: Transport commissioner Li Gu said, "Meng is a literary celebrity and is not practiced in clerical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Transport commissioner Li Gu explained, "Meng is a literary gentleman and is not accustomed to administrative work.

sentences.zh: 」遂不之問。

translations.literal: " He was therefore not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: " Congyi left him alone after that.

sentences.zh: 周廣順中，從歸德軍節度趙暉為掌書記，召為右拾遺、直史館、知制誥。

translations.literal: In the Guangshun era of Zhou he followed Guilde military commissioner Zhao Hui as secretarial aide and was summoned as Right Reminder, duty historian in the History Office, and drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhou Guangshun era he served as secretary to Zhao Hui, military governor of Guide, and was then summoned to the posts of right reminder, duty historian in the History Office, and drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 蒙從弟載時為翰林學士，兄弟並掌內外制，時號「二扈」。

translations.literal: Meng's younger cousin Zai was then Hanlin academician; the brothers together handled internal and external edicts, and at the time they were called "the two Hus."
translations.idiomatic: Meng's cousin Zai was then a Hanlin academician, and the two of them together handled palace and court edicts, earning the nickname "the two Hus."

sentences.zh: 宋初，由中書舍人遷翰林學士，坐請託於同年仇華，黜為太子左贊善大夫，稍遷左補闕，掌大名市征。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was transferred from Secretariat Drafter to Hanlin academician; he sat because of entreating favor for his examination-year fellow Qiu Hua, was demoted to Left Supporter of the Heir Apparent in the Eastern Palace, and gradually transferred to Left Remonstrator, in charge of market levies in Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he rose from secretariat drafter to Hanlin academician but was demoted to left supporter of the heir apparent for having solicited favors for his examination-year fellow Qiu Hua; he was later made left remonstrator and put in charge of market taxes at Daming.

sentences.zh: 六年，復知制誥，充史館修撰。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he again drafted edicts and served as compiler in the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of his reign he was restored to drafting edicts and appointed compiler in the History Office.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，受詔與李穆等同修《五代史》，詳定《古今本草》。

translations.literal: During Kaibao he received an edict with Li Mu and others jointly to compile the History of the Five Dynasties and to revise in detail the Comprehensive Materia Medica of Past and Present.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaibao era he was ordered to join Li Mu and others in compiling the History of the Five Dynasties and in revising the Comprehensive Materia Medica of Past and Present.

sentences.zh: 五年，連知貢舉。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he served consecutively as supervisor of the civil service examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he again supervised the civil service examinations.

sentences.zh: 七年，蒙上書言：「昔唐文宗每召大臣論事，必命起居郎、起居舍人執筆立於殿側，以紀時政，故《文宗實錄》稍為詳備。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Meng submitted a memorial saying, "Formerly Emperor Wenzong of Tang whenever summoned chief ministers to discuss affairs always ordered the Attendant of the Imperial Diary and Attendant of the Imperial Diary to hold brush and stand at the hall side to record current administration; therefore the Veritable Records of Wenzong are somewhat detailed and complete.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Meng memorialized, "In the Tang, whenever Emperor Wenzong summoned his ministers to discuss state affairs, he had the attendants of the imperial diary stand at the side of the hall with brush in hand to record what was said, which is why the Veritable Records of Emperor Wenzong are relatively full.

sentences.zh: 至後唐明宗，亦命端明殿學士及樞密直學士輪修日曆，送史官。

translations.literal: Down to Emperor Mingzong of Later Tang, he also ordered academicians of the Hall of Illustrious Brightness and direct academicians of the Bureau of Military Affairs to take turns compiling the daily calendar and send it to the historiographers.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Tang Emperor Mingzong as well, academicians of the Hall of Illustrious Brightness and direct academicians of the Bureau of Military Affairs were ordered to compile the court diary in rotation and submit it to the historiographers.

sentences.zh: 近來此事都廢，每季雖有內殿日曆，樞密院錄送史館，然所記者不過臣下對見辭謝而已。

translations.literal: In recent times this matter has all been abandoned; although each season there is an inner-palace daily calendar and the Bureau of Military Affairs records sent to the History Office, what is recorded is nothing more than subordinates' audiences, farewells, and thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Recently this practice has fallen into complete disuse; although each quarter an inner-palace diary and records from the Bureau of Military Affairs are still sent to the History Office, they note nothing beyond officials' audiences, leave-takings, and expressions of gratitude.

sentences.zh: 帝王言動，莫得而書。

translations.literal: The ruler's words and actions cannot be written.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's own words and deeds go unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 緣宰相以漏泄為虞，昧於宣播；

translations.literal: Because chief ministers take leakage as a worry, they are dim regarding dissemination;
translations.idiomatic: Because chief ministers fear leaks, they are reluctant to circulate information;

sentences.zh: 史官疏遠，何得與聞。

translations.literal: historiographers are distant and removed—how could they hear and know.
translations.idiomatic: and the historiographers stand too far outside the inner circle to learn what happened.

sentences.zh: 望自今凡有裁制之事，優恤之言，發自宸衷、可書簡策者，並委宰臣及參知政事每月輪知抄錄，以備史官撰集。

translations.literal: I hope that from now on whenever there are matters of decision, words of favor and relief, or utterances from the imperial heart fit to be written on bamboo and silk, all be entrusted to chief ministers and participants in governance to take monthly turns copying and recording, to supply the historiographers' compilation.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that henceforth all decisions, expressions of favor, and other pronouncements from the imperial heart worthy of the historical record be entrusted to the chief ministers and vice directors of the Secretariat to copy in monthly rotation for the historiographers' use.

sentences.zh: 」從之，即以參知政事盧多遜典其事。

translations.literal: " The request was approved, and Vice Director of the Secretariat Lu Duoxun was immediately put in charge of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed and placed Vice Director Lu Duoxun in charge of the project.

sentences.zh: 九年正月，受朝乾元殿，降王在列，聲明大備。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year he received court at the Hall of Qianyuan; surrendered kings were in the ranks and ceremonial music was fully prepared.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the ninth year the court assembled in the Hall of Qianyuan with the surrendered kings in attendance and full ceremonial music.

sentences.zh: 蒙上《聖功頌》，以述太祖受禪、平一天下之功，其詞誇麗，有詔褒之。

translations.literal: Meng presented "Ode to Sagely Achievement" describing Taizu's receiving the abdication and pacifying all under Heaven; its wording was boastful and ornate, and an edict praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Meng submitted his "Ode to Sagely Achievement," praising Taizu's acceptance of the abdication and unification of the realm; though the language was florid, an edict commended it.

sentences.zh: 為盧多遜所惡，出知江陵府。

translations.literal: He was hated by Lu Duoxun and was sent out to govern Jiangling Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Duoxun took a dislike to him, and he was sent out to serve as prefect of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，召拜中書舍人，旋復翰林學士。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne he was summoned and appointed Secretariat Drafter, and shortly restored as Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong succeeded to the throne he was recalled as secretariat drafter and soon restored to the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 與李昉同修《太祖實錄》。

translations.literal: Together with Li Fang he compiled the Veritable Records of Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Li Fang in compiling the Veritable Records of Taizu.

sentences.zh: 太平興國四年，從征太原還，轉戶部侍郎，加承旨。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo, returning from the campaign against Taiyuan, he was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue and added as Academician-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo, after returning from the Taiyuan campaign, he was made vice minister of revenue and chief Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，被疾，以工部尚書致仕。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi he fell ill and retired as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongxi he fell ill and retired with the rank of minister of works.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: Before long he died, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 贈右僕射。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 自張昭、竇儀卒，典章儀注，多蒙所刊定。

translations.literal: After Zhang Zhao and Dou Yi died, canonical regulations and ritual protocols were largely edited and fixed by Meng.
translations.idiomatic: After the deaths of Zhang Zhao and Dou Yi, most revisions to court regulations and ritual protocols were made by Meng.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖受周禪，追尊四廟，親郊，以宣祖配天。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Taizu received the Zhou abdication, he posthumously honored the four ancestral temples and personally performed suburban sacrifice, matching the Proclamation Ancestor with Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu first accepted the Zhou abdication, he enshrined four generations of ancestors and performed the suburban sacrifice in person, matching his great-grandfather the Proclamation Ancestor with Heaven.

sentences.zh: 及太宗即位，禮官以為舜郊嚳，商郊冥，周郊后稷，王業所因興也。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, ritual officials held that Shun sacrificed to Ku at the suburbs, Shang to Ming, Zhou to Hou Ji—these were the foundations from which royal enterprise arose.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong came to the throne, the ritual officials argued that Shun sacrificed to Ku, the Shang to Ming, and the Zhou to Hou Ji at the suburban rites—these were the ancestral spirits on whom each dynasty's kingship had been founded.

sentences.zh: 若漢高之太公，光武之南頓君，雖有帝父之尊，而無預配天之祭。

translations.literal: As for Han Gaozu's Grand Duke, Guangwu's Lord of Nandun—although they had the honor of the emperor's father, they had no part in the sacrifice matching with Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gaozu's father the Grand Duke and Guangwu's father the Lord of Nandun, though honored as imperial fathers, were never matched with Heaven in the suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 故自太平興國三年、六年再郊，並以太祖配，於禮為允。

translations.literal: Therefore from the third and sixth years of Taiping Xingguo, when suburban sacrifice was performed again, Taizu was matched in both—this was acceptable in ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Thus when suburban sacrifices were held again in the third and sixth years of Taiping Xingguo, matching Taizu with Heaven was ritually proper.

sentences.zh: 太宗將東封，蒙定議曰：「嚴父莫大於配天，請以宣祖配天。

translations.literal: When Taizong was about to perform the eastern Feng sacrifice, Meng fixed the deliberation saying, "Honoring the father—nothing is greater than matching with Heaven; I request that the Proclamation Ancestor be matched with Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong prepared to perform the Feng sacrifice on Mount Tai, Meng ruled that "nothing honors the father more than matching him with Heaven" and proposed matching the Proclamation Ancestor with Heaven.

sentences.zh: 」自雍熙元年罷封禪為郊祀，遂行其禮，識者非之。

translations.literal: " From the first year of Yongxi the Feng and Chan were abolished in favor of suburban sacrifice, and his ritual was carried out; knowledgeable persons criticized it.
translations.idiomatic: " After the Feng and Chan were abandoned in favor of suburban sacrifice in the first year of Yongxi, this arrangement was implemented, though scholars of ritual disapproved.

sentences.zh: 蒙性沉厚，不言人是非，好釋典，不喜殺，縉紳稱善人。

translations.literal: Meng's nature was deep and steady; he did not speak of others' right and wrong; he loved Buddhist scriptures and disliked killing; gentry and officials called him a good man.
translations.idiomatic: Meng was sober and steady, never gossiping about others, devoted to Buddhist texts and averse to bloodshed; the gentry praised him as a good man.

sentences.zh: 有笑疾，雖上前不自禁。

translations.literal: He had a laughing ailment and could not restrain himself even before the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He suffered from uncontrollable fits of laughter, which he could not suppress even in the emperor's presence.

sentences.zh: 多著述，有《鰲山集》二十卷行於世。

translations.literal: He wrote many works; his Collected Works from Aoshan in twenty juan circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He was a prolific author; his twenty-juan Collected Works from Aoshan circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 載字仲熙，有傳，見《五代史》

translations.literal: Zai, style name Zhongxi, has a biography—see the History of the Five Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Zai, styled Zhongxi, has a separate biography in the History of the Five Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 王著，字成象，單州單父人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhe, courtesy name Chenxiang, was a native of Shanfu in Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhe, styled Chenxiang, came from Shanfu in Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 性豁達，無城府。

translations.literal: His nature was open and generous, without hidden schemes.
translations.idiomatic: He was open-hearted and guileless.

sentences.zh: 幼能屬文，漢乾祐中，舉進士。

translations.literal: From youth he could compose essays; in the Qianyou era of Han he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He showed literary talent early and passed the jinshi examination during the Later Han Qianyou era.

sentences.zh: 周祖鎮大名，世宗侍行，聞著名，召置門下，因得謁見周祖。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder held Daming, Shizong attended him on the journey; hearing of Zhe's fame, he summoned him to his staff and thereby obtained audience with the Zhou founder.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou founder was posted at Daming, Shizong accompanied him and, hearing of Zhe's reputation, took him onto his staff, through which Zhe gained an audience with the Zhou founder.

sentences.zh: 廣順中，世宗鎮澶州，辟觀察支使。

translations.literal: In Guangshun, when Shizong held Cao Prefecture, he recruited him as surveillance commissioner aide.
translations.idiomatic: During Guangshun, when Shizong was posted at Cao Prefecture, he appointed Zhe surveillance commissioner aide.

sentences.zh: 隨世宗入朝，遷殿中丞；

translations.literal: Following Shizong to court, he was promoted to Palace Director;
translations.idiomatic: He followed Shizong to the capital and was promoted to palace director;

sentences.zh: 即位，拜度支員外郎。

translations.literal: when Shizong took the throne, he was appointed Vice Director of the Revenue Section.
translations.idiomatic: and when Shizong succeeded to the throne he was made vice director of the revenue section.

sentences.zh: 顯德三年，充翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiande he served as Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiande he was made a Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 六年，丁家艱，起復。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he entered mourning for family bereavement and was recalled from mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he went into mourning for a family death but was recalled to office before the mourning period ended.

sentences.zh: 南唐李景使其弟從善來貢，會恭帝嗣位，命著伴送至睢陽，加金部郎中、知制誥，賜金紫。

translations.literal: Southern Tang's Li Jing sent his younger brother Congshan to present tribute; it happened that Emperor Gong succeeded to the throne, and Zhe was ordered to accompany and escort him to Suiyang; he was added as Director of the Ministry of Revenue and drafter of edicts and granted gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: When Southern Tang's Li Jing sent his brother Congshan to present tribute, Emperor Gong had just succeeded to the throne; Zhe was ordered to escort the envoy to Suiyang, promoted to director in the Ministry of Revenue with responsibility for drafting edicts, and granted the gold-and-purple insignia.

sentences.zh: 世宗靈駕赴慶陵，符后從行，公務悉資於著。

translations.literal: When Shizong's imperial coffin went to Qing Mausoleum and Empress Fu accompanied the journey, all official business relied on Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong's funeral procession went to Qing Mausoleum with Empress Fu in attendance, Zhe handled all the official arrangements.

sentences.zh: 宋初，加中書舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was added as Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he was made secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，知貢舉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong he supervised the civil service examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianlong he supervised the civil service examinations.

sentences.zh: 時亳州獻紫芝，鄆州獲白兔，隴州貢黃鸚鵡，著獻頌，因以規諫。

translations.literal: At that time Bozhou presented purple fungus, Yan Prefecture obtained a white hare, and Long Prefecture offered a yellow parrot; Zhe presented a eulogy and thereby offered remonstrance and admonition.
translations.idiomatic: When Bozhou presented purple fungus, Yanzhou reported a white hare, and Longzhou offered a yellow parrot, Zhe submitted a eulogy that doubled as admonition.

sentences.zh: 太祖甚嘉其意，下詔褒之。

translations.literal: Taizu greatly approved his intent and issued an edict praising him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu greatly approved his intent and issued an edict commending him.

sentences.zh: 四年春，宿直禁中，被酒，髮倒垂被面，夜扣滋德殿門求見。

translations.literal: In spring of the fourth year, on night duty in the inner palace, he was drunk; his hair hung down covering his face, and at night he knocked on the Gate of Nurturing Virtue seeking audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year, while on night duty in the inner palace, he became drunk; his hair fell over his face, and in the night he knocked on the Gate of Nurturing Virtue demanding an audience.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，發其醉宿倡家之過，黜為比部員外郎。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, exposed his offense of drunkenly lodging in a singing-girl house, and demoted him to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, exposed his offense of spending the night drunk in a brothel, and demoted him to vice director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 乾德初，改兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qiande he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qiande he was transferred to vice director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 二年，復知制誥。

translations.literal: In the second year he again drafted edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was restored to drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 數月，加史館修撰、判館事。

translations.literal: Several months later he was added as compiler in the History Office and given charge of office affairs.
translations.idiomatic: A few months later he was made compiler in the History Office with charge of its affairs.

sentences.zh: 三年，就轉戶部郎中。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred in place to Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 六年，復為翰林學士，加兵部郎中，再知貢舉。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he again became Hanlin academician, was added as Director of the Ministry of War, and again supervised the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was restored to the Hanlin Academy, made director in the Ministry of War, and again supervised the civil service examinations.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年冬，暴卒，年四十二。

translations.literal: In winter of the second year of Kaibao he died suddenly, aged forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died suddenly in the winter of the second year of Kaibao at the age of forty-two.

sentences.zh: 著少有俊才，世宗以幕府舊僚，眷待尤厚，常召見與語，命皇子出拜，每呼學士而不名。

translations.literal: Zhe from youth had outstanding talent; Shizong, because he was an old staff member of the headquarters, favored him especially; he was often summoned to converse, ordered the princes to come out and bow, and always called him "Academician" without using his name.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe had shown exceptional talent from youth; Shizong, remembering him as an old member of his staff, treated him with special favor, often summoned him for conversation, had the princes bow to him, and always addressed him as "Academician" without using his personal name.

sentences.zh: 屢欲相之，以其嗜酒，故遲留久之。

translations.literal: He repeatedly wished to make him chief minister, but because of his love of wine he delayed for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong repeatedly intended to make him chief minister but kept putting it off because of his drinking.

sentences.zh: 及世宗疾大漸，太祖與范質入受顧命，謂質等曰：「王著藩邸舊人，我若不諱，當命為相。

translations.literal: When Shizong's illness grew critical, Taizu and Fan Zhi entered to receive the final command; he said to Zhi and others, "Wang Zhe is an old man of the princely establishment; if I do not demur, he ought to be appointed chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong's illness grew critical, Taizu and Fan Zhi came to receive his final instructions; he told Zhi and the others, "Wang Zhe is an old companion from my princely days; barring some obstacle, I would have made him chief minister.

sentences.zh: 」世宗崩乃止。

translations.literal: " When Shizong died the matter ceased.
translations.idiomatic: " After Shizong died, nothing came of it.

sentences.zh: 著善與人交，好延譽後進，當世士大夫稱之。

translations.literal: Zhe was good at making friends and loved to extend reputation to younger scholars; the gentry and officials of the age praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe was sociable and generous in promoting younger scholars; his contemporaries among the gentry spoke well of him.

sentences.zh: 有傳，見《五代史》。

translations.literal: He has a biography—see the History of the Five Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: He has a separate biography in the History of the Five Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 王祜，字景叔，大名莘人。

translations.literal: Wang Hu, courtesy name Jingshu, was a native of Shen in Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hu, styled Jingshu, came from Shen in Daming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖言，仕唐黎陽令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yan served as magistrate of Liyang under Tang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yan had served as magistrate of Liyang under the Tang.

sentences.zh: 父徹，舉後唐進士，至左拾遺。

translations.literal: His father Che passed the jinshi examination under Later Tang and rose to Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: His father Che passed the jinshi examination under Later Tang and rose to left remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 祜少篤志詞學，性倜儻有俊氣。

translations.literal: Hu from youth was devoted to literary studies; his nature was free and bold with outstanding spirit.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Hu devoted himself to letters and possessed a bold, spirited temperament.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，以書見桑維翰，稱其藻麗，由是名聞京師。

translations.literal: In the Tianfu era of Jin he presented a writing to Sang Weihan, who praised its literary elegance; thereby his name became known in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jin Tianfu era he submitted a literary work to Sang Weihan, who praised its elegance, and his reputation spread through the capital.

sentences.zh: 鄴帥杜重威辟為觀察支使。

translations.literal: The Ye military commissioner Du Chongwei recruited him as surveillance commissioner aide.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chongwei, military governor of Ye, recruited him as surveillance commissioner aide.

sentences.zh: 漢初，重威移鎮睢陽，反側不自安，祜嘗勸之，使無反漢，不聽。

translations.literal: Early in Han, Chongwei was transferred to hold Suiyang and was restless and ill at ease; Hu once urged him not to rebel against Han, but he did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Later Han, when Chongwei was transferred to Suiyang and grew restless, Hu urged him not to rebel against the Han court, but Chongwei would not listen.

sentences.zh: 祜坐是貶沁州司戶參軍，因作書貽鄉友以見志，辭氣俊邁，人多稱之。

translations.literal: Hu on this account was demoted to revenue clerk in Qin Prefecture; he therefore composed a letter sent to hometown friends to express his resolve; its wording was lofty and vigorous, and many people praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Hu was demoted to revenue clerk in Qinzhou for his association with Chongwei; he wrote a letter to hometown friends expressing his principles in lofty, vigorous language that won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 仕周，歷魏縣、南樂二令。

translations.literal: Serving Zhou, he successively held the magistracies of Wei County and Nanle.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou he served successively as magistrate of Wei County and Nanle.

sentences.zh: 太祖受禪，拜監察御史，由魏縣移知光州，遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: When Taizu received the abdication he was appointed Investigating Censor; from Wei County he was transferred to govern Guang Prefecture and promoted to Attending Censor in the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu accepted the abdication, Hu was made investigating censor, transferred from Wei County to govern Guang Prefecture, and then promoted to attending censor in the palace.

sentences.zh: 乾德三年，知制誥。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qiande he drafted edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Qiande he was put in charge of drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 六年，加集賢院修撰，轉戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was added as compiler in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made compiler in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 太祖征太原，已濟河。

translations.literal: When Taizu campaigned against Taiyuan, he had already crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu campaigned against Taiyuan, the army had already crossed the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 諸州饋集上黨城中，車乘塞路，上聞之，將以稽留罪轉運使。

translations.literal: Supplies from the prefectures gathered in Shangdang city; carts and carriages blocked the roads; when the emperor heard of it he was about to punish the transport commissioner for delay.
translations.idiomatic: Supplies from the prefectures piled up in Shangdang city until the roads were choked with wagons; when the emperor heard of it he was ready to punish the transport commissioner for the delay.

sentences.zh: 趙普曰：「六師方至，而轉運使以獲罪聞，敵必謂儲峙不充，有以窺我矣，非威遠之道也。

translations.literal: Zhao Pu said, "The six armies have just arrived, and if the transport commissioner is heard to have been punished, the enemy will surely think stores are insufficient and have means to spy on us—this is not the way to awe the distant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Pu said, "Our armies have only just arrived; if we punish the transport commissioner now, the enemy will think our supplies are inadequate and seize the chance to probe our weakness—that is no way to overawe distant foes.

sentences.zh: 俾能治劇者，往蒞其州足矣。

translations.literal: Let someone able to handle difficult affairs go to take charge of that prefecture—that is enough.
translations.idiomatic: Send someone capable of handling difficult assignments to take charge of that prefecture—that will suffice.

sentences.zh: 」即命祜知潞州。

translations.literal: " He immediately ordered Hu to govern Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor immediately appointed Hu prefect of Lu.

sentences.zh: 及至，饋餉無乏，路亦無壅，班師，召還。

translations.literal: When he arrived, provisions were not lacking and the roads were not blocked; when the army withdrew he was summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, supplies flowed without interruption and the roads were cleared; after the army withdrew he was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 會符彥卿鎮大名，頗不治，太祖以祜代之，俾察彥卿動靜，謂曰：「此卿故鄉，所謂晝錦者也。

translations.literal: It happened that Fu Yanqing held Daming and was quite neglectful in governance; Taizu replaced him with Hu and had him observe Yanqing's movements, saying to him, "This is your old hometown—the so-called 'returning in brocade by day.'
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Yanqing was posted at Daming and governed poorly, Taizu sent Hu to replace him and watch Yanqing's conduct, telling him, "This is your native place—the occasion for returning in glory.

sentences.zh: 」祜以百口明彥卿無罪，且曰：「五代之君，多因猜忌殺無辜，故享國不永，願陛下以為戒。

translations.literal: " Hu with a hundred mouths declared Yanqing innocent and moreover said, "The rulers of the Five Dynasties mostly killed the innocent out of suspicion, and therefore their possession of the state was not long; I wish Your Majesty to take this as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: " Hu swore on the lives of his entire household that Yanqing was innocent and added, "The rulers of the Five Dynasties often destroyed innocent men through suspicion, and their dynasties therefore did not endure; I beg Your Majesty to take warning from this.

sentences.zh: 」彥卿由是獲免，故世謂祜有陰德。

translations.literal: " Yanqing thereby escaped punishment; therefore the age said Hu had hidden virtue.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanqing was spared, and later generations said Hu had earned hidden merit.

sentences.zh: 繼以用兵嶺表，徙知襄州。

translations.literal: Subsequently, because of military use in the Lingnan region, he was transferred to govern Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When troops were sent to the Lingnan region, he was transferred to Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 湖湘平，移知潭州。

translations.literal: When Hunan was pacified he was transferred to govern Tan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After Hunan was pacified he was made prefect of Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 召還，攝判吏部銓。

translations.literal: He was summoned back and acted as adjudicator of the Ministry of Personnel selection.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and put in charge of personnel selection in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時左司員外郎侯陟自揚州還，復判銓，祜判門下省，陟所注擬，祜多駁正。

translations.literal: At that time Left Office Vice Director Hou Zhi returned from Yangzhou and again adjudicated selection; Hu adjudicated the Secretariat; Zhi's proposed appointments Hu often rejected and corrected.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Hou Zhi of the left office had returned from Yangzhou and resumed adjudicating selections; Hu handled appointments for the Secretariat and frequently overturned Zhi's nominations.

sentences.zh: 盧多遜與陟善，陟因訴之，多遜素惡祜不比己，遂出祜為鎮國軍行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Lu Duoxun was on good terms with Zhi; Zhi therefore complained to him; Duoxun had long hated Hu for not siding with him, and thus sent Hu out as administrative aide on the Zhenguo army staff.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Duoxun was friendly with Zhi, and Zhi complained to him; Duoxun had long resented Hu for refusing to align with him and had Hu sent out as administrative aide on the staff of the Zhenguo army.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，移知河中府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he was transferred to govern Hezhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taiping Xingguo he was transferred to Hezhong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 入為左司員外郎，拜中書舍人，充史館修撰。

translations.literal: He entered court as Left Office Vice Director, was appointed Secretariat Drafter, and served as compiler in the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as vice director of the left office, made secretariat drafter, and appointed compiler in the History Office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，知開封府，以病請告。

translations.literal: Before long he governed Kaifeng Prefecture and requested leave on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was put in charge of Kaifeng Prefecture but requested sick leave.

sentences.zh: 太宗謂祜文章、清節兼著，特拜兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Taizong said Hu was distinguished in both literary work and pure integrity and specially appointed him Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong, noting Hu's literary distinction and integrity, specially promoted him to vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 月餘卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: After more than a month he died, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died a little over a month later at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 初，祜掌誥，會盧多遜為學士，陰傾趙普，多遜累諷祜比己，祜不從。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Hu handled edicts, it happened that Lu Duoxun was academician and secretly worked against Zhao Pu; Duoxun repeatedly hinted that Hu should side with him, but Hu did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu was drafting edicts, Hanlin academician Lu Duoxun was secretly working to undermine Zhao Pu and repeatedly urged Hu to join him, but Hu refused.

sentences.zh: 一日，以宇文融排張說事勸釋之，多遜滋不悅。

translations.literal: One day he used the affair of Yuwen Rong driving out Zhang Yue to urge him to desist; Duoxun grew still more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: One day Hu cited Yuwen Rong's persecution of Zhang Yue as a warning, which only deepened Duoxun's resentment.

sentences.zh: 及普再入，多遜果敗，與宇文融事頗類，識者服其先見。

translations.literal: When Pu returned to power, Duoxun indeed fell; it resembled the Yuwen Rong affair rather closely, and knowledgeable persons admired Hu's foresight.
translations.idiomatic: When Pu returned to power, Duoxun indeed fell—a outcome much like the Yuwen Rong affair—and observers admired Hu's foresight.

sentences.zh: 祜子三人：曰懿，曰旦，曰旭。

translations.literal: Hu had three sons: named Yi, Dan, and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Hu had three sons: Yi, Dan, and Xu.

sentences.zh: 旦自有傳。

translations.literal: Dan has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Dan has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 初，祜知貢舉，多拔擢寒俊，畢士安、柴成務皆其所取也，後與其子旦同入兩制，居中書。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Hu supervised the examinations, he promoted many poor but talented men; Bi Shian and Chai Chengwu were among those he selected; later he and his son Dan both entered the two drafting offices and held posts in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu supervised the examinations he promoted many talented men from humble backgrounds, including Bi Shian and Chai Chengwu; later he and his son Dan both served in the drafting offices and reached the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 懿，字文德，勵志為學，舉進士，嘗知袁州，有政績，卒，年四十九。

translations.literal: Yi, style name Wende, was devoted to learning, passed the jinshi examination, once governed Yuan Prefecture with administrative achievements, and died aged forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, styled Wende, devoted himself to scholarship, passed the jinshi examination, served as prefect of Yuanzhou with distinction, and died at forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 子 旭

translations.literal: Son Xu
translations.idiomatic: His son Xu

sentences.zh: 旭字仲明。

translations.literal: Xu, style name Zhongming.
translations.idiomatic: Xu, styled Zhongming.

sentences.zh: 嚴於治內，恕以接物，尤篤友誼。

translations.literal: Strict in governing the household, lenient in dealing with others, especially devoted in friendship.
translations.idiomatic: He was strict in managing his household but lenient toward others and especially loyal in friendship.

sentences.zh: 以蔭補太祝，嘗知緱氏縣。

translations.literal: By yin privilege he was appointed Grand Sacrificer and once governed Gou Clan County.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service by yin privilege as grand sacrificer and once served as magistrate of Gou Clan County.

sentences.zh: 時官鄰邑者多貪猥，民有「永寧三钁，緱氏一鎌」之謠。

translations.literal: At the time officials in neighboring counties were mostly greedy and base, and the people had a saying: "Three hoes in Yongning, one sickle in Gou Clan County."
translations.idiomatic: Officials in nearby counties were notoriously corrupt and grasping, and the people sang: "Yongning needs three hoes, Gou Clan County needs but one sickle."

sentences.zh: 又知雍丘縣。

translations.literal: He also governed Yongqiu County.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as magistrate of Yongqiu County as well.

sentences.zh: 真宗尹京時，素聞其能，及踐阼，三遷至殿中丞。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong governed the capital as heir apparent, he had long heard of Xu's ability; when he acceded to the throne, Xu was promoted three times to Palace Bureau Director.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong had already heard of Xu's talents while serving as heir apparent in the capital, and after his accession he promoted Xu three times until he reached the rank of palace bureau director.

sentences.zh: 自旦居宰府，旭以嫌不任職。

translations.literal: From the time Dan held the chief ministry, Xu because of conflict of interest did not hold office.
translations.idiomatic: Once Dan became chief minister, Xu stopped taking office to avoid the appearance of nepotism.

sentences.zh: 王矩嘗薦旭材堪治劇，真宗召旦謂曰：「前代弟兄同居要地者多矣，朝廷任才，豈以卿故屈之邪？

translations.literal: Wang Ju once recommended Xu as having talent fit for heavy duties; Zhenzong summoned Dan and said: "In former ages brothers dwelling together in important posts were many; the court appoints talent—would it demean him because of you?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ju once recommended Xu as capable of handling demanding posts, and Zhenzong summoned Dan and said, "Brothers have often held high office together in past dynasties. The court appoints men for their ability—surely it would not hold your brother back on your account?"

sentences.zh: 」命授京府推官，旦固辭，改判南曹。

translations.literal: He ordered Xu appointed investigator of the capital prefecture; Dan firmly declined, and the appointment was changed to vice director of the Southern Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered Xu appointed as an investigator for the capital prefecture, but Dan firmly declined the post, and Xu was instead assigned as vice director of the Southern Bureau.

sentences.zh: 由判國子監出知潁州，荒政修舉。

translations.literal: From serving as vice director of the Directorate of Education he went out to govern Ying Prefecture, where famine relief was well carried out.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as vice director of the Directorate of Education, he was sent out to govern Ying Prefecture, where he organized famine relief with notable success.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符間，旦既薨，敭歷中外，卓有政績，由兵部郎中出知應天府。

translations.literal: During the Dazhong Xiangfu era, after Dan had died, Xu served inside and outside the court with outstanding administrative achievements; from Bureau Director in the Ministry of War he went out to govern Yingtian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dazhong Xiangfu period, after Dan's death, Xu served in both central and local posts with distinguished achievements, and from his post as bureau director in the Ministry of War he was appointed prefect of Yingtian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: He died, aged sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 懿子睦，旭子質，皆能其官。

translations.literal: Yi's son Mu and Xu's son Zhi both were capable in their offices.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's son Mu and Xu's son Zhi both proved themselves fully equal to their duties.

sentences.zh: 孫 質

translations.literal: Son Zhi
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhi

sentences.zh: 質，字子野。

translations.literal: Zhi, style name Ziye.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, styled Ziye.

sentences.zh: 少謹厚淳約，力學問，師事楊億，億歎以為英妙。

translations.literal: From youth he was careful, honest, plain, and restrained; he devoted himself to learning and took Yang Yi as his teacher; Yi sighed in admiration that he was extraordinarily brilliant.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he was careful, honest, and unpretentious, and he applied himself to scholarship under Yang Yi, who marveled at his exceptional talent.

sentences.zh: 伯父旦見其所為文，嗟賞之。

translations.literal: His uncle Dan saw essays he had written and sighed in admiration of them.
translations.idiomatic: When his uncle Dan read his essays, he praised them with deep admiration.

sentences.zh: 以蔭補太常寺奉禮郎。

translations.literal: By yin privilege he was appointed a ceremonial officer of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service by yin privilege as a ceremonial officer in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 後獻文召試，賜進士及第，被薦為館閣校勘，改集賢校理，累遷尚書祠部員外郎。

translations.literal: Later he submitted writings for a summoned examination, was granted jinshi with highest honors, was recommended as an archives collator, changed to collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and was promoted to assistant department director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He later submitted his writings for a palace examination, passed the jinshi with highest honors, was recommended as an archives collator, then served as a collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and rose to assistant department director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，與諸弟飯脫粟茹蔬。

translations.literal: When in mourning for his father, he and his younger brothers ate husked millet and plain vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning his father, he and his younger brothers lived on husked millet and vegetables alone.

sentences.zh: 終喪，通判蘇州，州守黃宗旦少質，嘗因爭事，宗旦曰：「少年乃與丈人抗邪？

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he served as judicial intendant of Suzhou; the prefect Huang Zongdan looked down on Zhi because he was young; once in disputing an affair, Zongdan said: "A youth contending with an elder?"
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he served as judicial intendant of Suzhou, where Prefect Huang Zongdan looked down on him for his youth; once during a dispute Zongdan said, "How dare a young man stand up to his senior?"

sentences.zh: 」質曰：「事有當爭，職也。

translations.literal: Zhi said: "When matters must be disputed, it is one's duty."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi replied, "When a matter ought to be contested, that is simply doing one's duty."

sentences.zh: 」卒不為屈。

translations.literal: In the end he did not yield.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to back down.

sentences.zh: 宗旦得盜鑄錢者百餘人，下獄治，退告質曰：「吾以術鉤致得之。

translations.literal: Zongdan captured more than a hundred counterfeiters, sent them to prison for prosecution, and afterward told Zhi: "I obtained them by using stratagems to lure them in."
translations.idiomatic: Zongdan arrested more than a hundred counterfeiters and had them imprisoned for trial; afterward he told Zhi with satisfaction, "I caught them by setting a trap."

sentences.zh: 」喜見於色。

translations.literal: His pleasure showed on his face.
translations.idiomatic: His delight was plain to see.

sentences.zh: 質曰：「以術鉤人置之死而又喜，仁者之政，固如是乎？

translations.literal: Zhi said: "Using stratagems to ensnare people and send them to death and yet being pleased—is governance of the benevolent truly like this?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhi said, "You trap men with schemes, send them to their deaths, and then rejoice—is that what benevolent government looks like?"

sentences.zh: 」宗旦慚沮，為薄其罪。

translations.literal: Zongdan was ashamed and downcast and reduced their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed and abashed, Zongdan lightened their sentences.

sentences.zh: 還判尚書刑部、吏部南曹，知蔡州。

translations.literal: He returned to serve as vice director of the Ministry of Justice and the Southern Bureau of the Ministry of Personnel, and governed Cai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as vice director of the Ministry of Justice and the Southern Bureau of the Ministry of Personnel, and then appointed prefect of Cai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 州人歲時祀吳元濟廟，質曰：「安有逆醜而廟食於民者。

translations.literal: The people of the prefecture yearly sacrificed at the temple of Wu Yuanji; Zhi said: "How can there be a rebellious villain receiving temple offerings from the people?"
translations.idiomatic: Each year the people of the prefecture made offerings at the temple of Wu Yuanji, but Zhi said, "How can a rebel and traitor be worshipped by the people?"

sentences.zh: 」毀之，為更立狄仁傑、李愬像而祠之，蔡人至今號「雙廟」。

translations.literal: He destroyed it, rebuilt it with images of Di Renjie and Li Su for worship, and the people of Cai to this day call it the "Twin Temples."
translations.idiomatic: He tore the temple down and rebuilt it with images of Di Renjie and Li Su for worship, and the people of Cai still call it the "Twin Temples."

sentences.zh: 以本曹郎中召為開封府推官。

translations.literal: From department director of his bureau he was summoned as investigator of the Kaifeng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: From his post as bureau director he was recalled to serve as an investigator for the Kaifeng prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時兄雍為三司判官，質不欲兄弟並居省府，懇辭，得知壽州，徙廬州。

translations.literal: At that time his elder brother Yong was a judicial officer of the Three Departments; Zhi did not wish both brothers to serve together in the capital departments, earnestly declined, and was appointed to govern Shou Prefecture, then transferred to Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Yong was then a judicial officer of the Three Departments, and Zhi, unwilling to have both brothers serving together in the capital offices, declined the post and was instead appointed prefect of Shou Prefecture, then transferred to Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 盜殺其徒，并貲而遁，捕得之。

translations.literal: A bandit killed his companions, took all their goods, and fled; he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: A bandit killed his fellows, seized their goods, and fled, but was eventually caught.

sentences.zh: 質論盜死，大理以謂法不當死，質曰：「盜殺其徒，自首者原之，所以疑懷其黨，且許之自新，此法意也。

translations.literal: Zhi argued the bandit should die; the Court of Judicial Review said the law did not warrant death; Zhi said: "When a bandit kills his companions, those who surrender are pardoned—in order to arouse suspicion among his band and to allow them to renew themselves—such is the intent of the law."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi argued that the bandit deserved death, but the Court of Judicial Review held that the law did not require it; Zhi said, "The law pardons bandits who kill their companions only if they surrender voluntarily, so as to sow distrust among their fellows and give them a chance to reform—that is the law's purpose."

sentences.zh: 今殺人取貲而捕獲，貸之，豈法意乎？

translations.literal: Now he killed people, took goods, and was captured—if he is pardoned, is that the intent of the law?
translations.idiomatic: But this man murdered his companions, seized their property, and was captured in flight—if he is pardoned now, how does that serve the law's intent?

sentences.zh: 」疏上，不報，降監舒州靈仙觀。

translations.literal: The memorial went up; there was no response; he was demoted to superintendent of the Lingxian Abbey in Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial went unanswered, and he was demoted to superintendent of the Lingxian Abbey in Shuzhou.

sentences.zh: 採古今煉形攝生之術，撰《寶元總錄》百卷。

translations.literal: He collected ancient and modern methods of refining the body and preserving life, and compiled the "Comprehensive Record of the Baoyuan Era" in one hundred juan.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered methods of body cultivation and longevity from antiquity and his own day, and wrote the "Comprehensive Record of the Baoyuan Era" in one hundred juan.

sentences.zh: 逾年，韓琦知審刑院，請盜殺其徒，非自首者勿原，著為令。

translations.literal: More than a year later, Han Qi directed the Court of Judicial Review and requested that when bandits kill their companions, those who do not surrender should not be pardoned, establishing this as a statute.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later, Han Qi, as director of the Court of Judicial Review, petitioned that bandits who kill their companions should not be pardoned unless they surrender voluntarily, and this was enacted as law.
