sentences.zh: 於是鄭戩、葉清臣皆言質非罪，且稱其材，起知泰州，遷度支郎中，徙荊湖北路轉運使。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zheng Xian and Ye Qingchen both said Zhi was innocent of crime and also praised his talent; he was restored to govern Taizhou, promoted to Bureau Director of the Treasury, and transferred to transport commissioner of the Jinghu North circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xian and Ye Qingchen then declared that Zhi had committed no crime and praised his abilities; he was restored to office as prefect of Taizhou, promoted to bureau director of the treasury, and appointed transport commissioner for the Jinghu North circuit.

sentences.zh: 嘗攝江陵府事，或訴民約婚後期，民言貧無貲以辦，故違約。

translations.literal: Once while acting on Jiangling prefectural affairs, someone sued a man for breaking a marriage engagement past the deadline; the man said he was poor without funds to arrange it, hence breached the agreement.
translations.idiomatic: While temporarily handling affairs at Jiangling Prefecture, he heard a suit against a man who had missed the deadline for a betrothal; the man explained that poverty left him without the means to proceed, and so he had broken the engagement.

sentences.zh: 質問其費幾何，出私錢予之。

translations.literal: Zhi asked how much the costs would be and gave him money from his private funds.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi asked what the expenses would come to and paid them out of his own purse.

sentences.zh: 吏捕盜人衣者，盜叩頭曰：「平生不為過，迫饑寒而至於此。

translations.literal: An official caught a thief who stole clothes; the thief kowtowed and said: "In my whole life I have done no wrong; driven by hunger and cold I came to this."
translations.idiomatic: When an official arrested a man for stealing clothes, the thief kowtowed and said, "I have never done wrong before; hunger and cold drove me to this."

sentences.zh: 」質命取衣衣之，遣去。

translations.literal: Zhi ordered clothes taken and given to clothe him, and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi had clothes brought to dress him and let him go.

sentences.zh: 加史館修撰、同判吏部流內銓。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed Hanlin historiographer and co-director of the Ministry of Personnel's stream-within selection board.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made a historiographer of the History Office and co-director of the Ministry of Personnel's stream-within selection board.

sentences.zh: 擢天章閣待制，出知陝州，卒。

translations.literal: He was promoted to gentleman awaiting appointment at the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations, went out to govern Shan Prefecture, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to gentleman awaiting appointment at the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations, he was sent out to govern Shan Prefecture, where he died.

sentences.zh: 質家世富貴，兄弟習為驕侈，而質克己好善，自奉簡素如寒士，不喜畜財，至不能自給。

translations.literal: Zhi's family for generations had been wealthy and noble; his brothers were accustomed to arrogance and luxury, but Zhi restrained himself and loved goodness, maintaining himself simply like a poor scholar, disliking accumulation of wealth, to the point he could not supply his own needs.
translations.idiomatic: Though Zhi came from a wealthy and eminent family and his brothers lived in accustomed luxury, he disciplined himself, loved what was good, and kept to a plain life like a poor scholar; he refused to hoard wealth and sometimes could barely support himself.

sentences.zh: 初，旦為中書舍人，家貧，與昆弟貸人息錢，違期，以所乘馬償之。

translations.literal: Initially when Dan was a Secretariat drafter, the family was poor; he and his brothers borrowed interest-bearing money from others, missed the deadline, and repaid with the horse he rode.
translations.idiomatic: In the early days, when Dan was a Secretariat drafter, the family was so poor that he and his brothers borrowed money at interest; when they missed the repayment date, they settled the debt with the horse Dan rode.

sentences.zh: 質閱書得故券，召子弟示之曰：「此吾家素風，爾曹當毋忘也。

translations.literal: Zhi while reading found the old contract, summoned the young clansmen to show them, and said: "This is our family's longstanding way—you must not forget it."
translations.idiomatic: While reading one day, Zhi came upon the old contract; he gathered the younger members of the family and said, "This is the spirit of our house—never forget it."

sentences.zh: 」范仲淹貶饒州，治朋黨方急，質獨載酒往餞。

translations.literal: Fan Zhongyan was demoted to Raozhou; persecution of factional cliques was intense; Zhi alone took wine to see him off.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Zhongyan was exiled to Raozhou at the height of the campaign against factional cliques, Zhi alone went with wine to bid him farewell.

sentences.zh: 或以誚質，質曰：「范公賢者，得為之黨，幸矣。

translations.literal: Some mocked Zhi; Zhi said: "Master Fan is a worthy man—to be counted among his faction is fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: When some ridiculed him for it, Zhi said, "Master Fan is a man of worth; to be counted among his associates would be an honor."

sentences.zh: 」世以此益賢之。

translations.literal: The world for this regarded him even more as worthy.
translations.idiomatic: People admired him all the more for it.

sentences.zh: 楊昭儉

translations.literal: Yang Zhaojian.
translations.idiomatic: Next is Yang Zhaojian.

sentences.zh: 楊昭儉，字仲寶，京兆長安人。

translations.literal: Yang Zhaojian, style name Zhongbao, was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhaojian, styled Zhongbao, came from Chang'an in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 曾祖嗣復，唐門下侍郎、平章事、吏部尚書。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Sifu was Tang Vice Director of the Secretariat, Grand Councillor, and Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Sifu had served the Tang as vice director of the Secretariat, grand councillor, and minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 祖授，唐刑部尚書。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shou was Tang Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shou had been Tang minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 父景，梁左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: His father Jing was Liang Left Remonstrance Bureau Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jing had served the Liang as left remonstrance bureau grand master.

sentences.zh: 昭儉少敏俊，後唐長興中，登進士第。

translations.literal: Zhaojian in youth was sharp and talented; in Changxing of Later Tang he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaojian was quick and brilliant as a youth, and during the Changxing era of Later Tang he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 解褐成德軍節度推官。

translations.literal: Upon leaving office cloth he became military investigator of the Chengde circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as a military investigator on the staff of the Chengde circuit.

sentences.zh: 歷鎮、魏掌書記，拜左拾遺、直史館，與中書舍人張昭遠等同修《明宗實錄》。

translations.literal: He served as secretary at Zhen and Wei, was appointed Left Reminder and duty historian, and with Secretariat drafter Zhang Zhaoyuan and others compiled the "Veritable Records of Emperor Mingzong."
translations.idiomatic: He served as secretary at Zhen and Wei, was appointed left reminder and duty historian, and joined Secretariat drafter Zhang Zhaoyuan and others in compiling the "Veritable Records of Emperor Mingzong."

sentences.zh: 書成，遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: When the book was complete, he was transferred to Palace Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished, he was promoted to palace attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 天福初，改禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: Early in Tianfu he was changed to Assistant Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianfu era he was appointed assistant director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 晉祖命宰相馮道為契丹冊禮使，以昭儉為介，授職方員外郎，旋加虞部郎中，俄以本官知制誥。

translations.literal: The Jin founding emperor ordered Chief Minister Feng Dao to serve as envoy for Khitan investiture rites, with Zhaojian as deputy; he was appointed Assistant Director of the Bureau of Appointments, shortly added Bureau Director of the Forestry Bureau, and soon with that rank served as drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin founder appointed Chief Minister Feng Dao envoy for the Khitan investiture mission with Zhaojian as his deputy; Zhaojian was made assistant director of the Bureau of Appointments, then bureau director of the forestry bureau, and soon afterward was given the concurrent duty of drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 不逾月三拜命，時人榮之。

translations.literal: Within less than a month he received three appointments; people of the time gloried in it.
translations.idiomatic: In less than a month he received three appointments in succession, to the envy of his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 又為荊南高從誨生辰國信使，賜金紫。

translations.literal: He also served as birthday envoy to Gao Conghui of Jingnan and was granted gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as birthday envoy to Gao Conghui of Jingnan and was awarded the gold-and-purple insignia of high rank.

sentences.zh: 使回，拜中書舍人，又為翰林學士。

translations.literal: On return from the mission he was appointed Secretariat drafter and also Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from the mission he was appointed Secretariat drafter and also made a Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 時驕將張彥澤鎮涇原，暴殺從事張式，朝廷不加罪。

translations.literal: At the time the arrogant general Zhang Yanze was stationed at Jingyuan and violently killed staff member Zhang Shi; the court did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the overbearing general Zhang Yanze, stationed at Jingyuan, had brutally murdered his staff officer Zhang Shi, yet the court imposed no punishment.

sentences.zh: 昭儉與刑部郎中李濤、諫議大夫鄭受益抗疏論列，請置之法。

translations.literal: Zhaojian, together with Bureau Director Li Tao of the Ministry of Justice and Remonstrance Bureau Grand Master Zheng Shouyi, submitted a confrontational memorial enumerating the faults and requesting that he be punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaojian joined Bureau Director Li Tao of the Ministry of Justice and Remonstrance Bureau Grand Master Zheng Shouyi in a forceful memorial detailing the crime and demanding that Zhang be punished according to law.

sentences.zh: 疏奏不報。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: Their memorial received no reply.

sentences.zh: 會有詔令朝臣轉對，或有封事，亦許以不時條奏。

translations.literal: There happened to be an edict ordering court officials to rotate in audience, and if they had sealed memorials, they were also permitted to submit items out of schedule.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered court officials to take turns addressing the throne, and also allowed sealed memorials to be submitted at any time.

sentences.zh: 昭儉復上疏曰：「天子君臨四海，日有萬機，懋建諍臣，彌縫其闕。

translations.literal: Zhaojian again submitted a memorial saying: "The Son of Heaven oversees the four seas; daily there are myriad affairs; earnestly establish remonstrating ministers to mend its gaps."
translations.idiomatic: Zhaojian submitted another memorial: "The Son of Heaven rules the four seas and faces ten thousand affairs each day; remonstrating ministers should be established to repair the court's failings."

sentences.zh: 今則諫臣雖設，言路不通，藥石之論不達於聖聰，而邪佞之徒取容於左右。

translations.literal: Now remonstrators exist in name but the path of speech is blocked; stone-and-medicine remonstrances do not reach sacred hearing, while flatterers and sycophants gain favor at left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Yet though remonstrators exist in name, the path of candid speech is blocked; honest counsel never reaches the emperor's ears, while sycophants win favor at his side.

sentences.zh: 御史臺紀綱之府，彈糾之司，銜冤者固當昭雪，為蠹者難免放流。

translations.literal: The Censorate is the office of discipline, the bureau of impeachment; those bearing injustice should be cleared, and parasites should not escape demotion and exile.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate exists to uphold discipline and investigate wrongdoing; the wronged ought to be vindicated, and corrupt officials ought to be punished with demotion and exile.

sentences.zh: 陛下臨御以來，寬仁太甚，徒置兩司，殆如虛器。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty's rule, kindness and leniency have been excessive; the two bureaus exist in vain, nearly like empty vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty took the throne, excessive leniency has rendered both offices little more than empty titles.

sentences.zh: 遂令節使慢侮朝章，屠害幕吏，始訴冤於丹闕，反執送於本藩。

translations.literal: Thus military commissioners insult court regulations and slaughter staff officers; they first plead injustice at the vermillion gate but are instead escorted back to their province.
translations.idiomatic: The result is that military commissioners scorn the laws of the court and butcher their staff; victims who appeal for justice at the palace gates are sent back to the very provinces that wronged them.

sentences.zh: 苟安跋扈之心，莫恤冤抑之苦。

translations.literal: Secure in arrogance, heedless of the suffering of suppressed injustice.
translations.idiomatic: They rest secure in their arrogance and give no thought to the anguish of those whose grievances are suppressed.

sentences.zh: 願回睿斷，誅彥澤以謝軍吏。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would turn divine judgment and execute Yanze to appease the army officers.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to act with resolute judgment and execute Yanze to satisfy the officers and men.

sentences.zh: 」由是權臣忌之。

translations.literal: For this powerful ministers resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful ministers therefore came to resent him.

sentences.zh: 會請告洛陽，不赴晉祖喪，為有司所糾，停官。

translations.literal: It happened that he requested leave in Luoyang and did not attend the Jin founding emperor's funeral; he was impeached by the authorities and suspended from office.
translations.idiomatic: He happened to be on leave in Luoyang and failed to attend the Jin founder's funeral; the authorities impeached him and he was stripped of his post.

sentences.zh: 未幾，起為河南少尹，改秘書少監，尋復中書舍人。

translations.literal: Before long he was restored as Vice Governor of Henan, changed to Vice Director of the Secretariat, and soon again made Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was restored as vice governor of Henan, then made vice director of the Secretariat, and soon returned to his post as Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 時河決數郡，大發丁夫，以本部帥董其役，既而塞之。

translations.literal: At the time the Yellow River breached in several prefectures; laborers were conscripted in great numbers; the local commander supervised the work, and afterward it was sealed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River broke its banks in several prefectures, corvée labor was mobilized on a vast scale under the local commander, and the breach was eventually closed.

sentences.zh: 晉少主喜，詔立碑記其事。

translations.literal: The Jin young lord was pleased and ordered a stele erected to record the affair.
translations.idiomatic: The young Jin emperor was delighted and ordered a stele erected to commemorate the achievement.

sentences.zh: 昭儉表諫曰：「陛下刻石紀功，不若降哀痛之詔；

translations.literal: Zhaojian submitted a memorial remonstrating: "Your Majesty carving stone to record merit is not as good as issuing an edict of mourning and pain;"
translations.idiomatic: Zhaojian remonstrated in a memorial: "Your Majesty, rather than carving stone to celebrate success, it would be better to issue an edict expressing grief and concern;"

sentences.zh: 摛翰頌美，不若頒罪己之文。

translations.literal: wielding the brush to praise is not as good as promulgating an essay of self-blame.
translations.idiomatic: rather than wielding the brush in praise, it would be better to publish a proclamation of self-reproach."

sentences.zh: 」言甚切至，少主嗟賞之，卒罷其事。

translations.literal: His words were extremely earnest; the young lord sighed in admiration, and ultimately abandoned the affair.
translations.idiomatic: His words were forceful and sincere; the young emperor sighed in admiration and ultimately abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 周世宗愛其才，復召入翰林為學士。

translations.literal: Later Zhou Emperor Shizong admired his talent and again summoned him into the Hanlin as academician.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong of Later Zhou admired his talent and recalled him to the Hanlin Academy as an academician.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，改御史中丞，多振舉臺憲故事。

translations.literal: After a year and more he was changed to Censor-in-Chief and revived many censorate traditions.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a year he was made censor-in-chief and restored many long-neglected censorate practices.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以鞫獄之失，與知雜御史趙礪、侍御史張糾並出為武勝軍節度行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Before long, for errors in trying cases, together with supervising censor Zhao Li and attendant censor Zhang Jiu he was all demoted to traveling vice marshal of the Wusheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, because of errors in adjudicating cases, he was demoted together with supervising censor Zhao Li and attendant censor Zhang Jiu to traveling vice marshal of the Wusheng Army.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，入為太子詹事，以眼疾求退。

translations.literal: In Kaibao year 2 he entered service as Tutor of the Heir Apparent and requested retirement due to eye illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaibao he was appointed tutor of the heir apparent, but he requested retirement because of failing eyesight.

sentences.zh: 六年，以工部尚書致仕。

translations.literal: In year 6 he retired as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he retired with the rank of minister of works.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，就加禮部尚書。

translations.literal: When Taizong acceded to the throne, he was concurrently promoted to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, Zhaojian was further honored with the title of minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，卒，年七十六。

translations.literal: In Taiping Xingguo year 2 he died, aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Taiping Xingguo at the age of seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 昭儉美風儀，善談名理，事晉有直聲。

translations.literal: Zhaojian had fine bearing, was skilled at discussing principles, and had a reputation for uprightness under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaojian had an elegant bearing, spoke well on philosophical principles, and won a reputation for integrity under the Jin.

sentences.zh: 然利口喜譏訾，執政大臣懼其構謗，多曲徇其意。

translations.literal: Yet he was sharp-tongued and fond of satire and blame; ruling ministers feared his slander and often indulged his wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he had a sharp tongue and loved to mock and criticize; the chief ministers feared his attacks and often humored him.

sentences.zh: 魚崇諒

translations.literal: Yu Chongliang.
translations.idiomatic: Next is Yu Chongliang.

sentences.zh: 魚崇諒，字仲益，其先楚州山陽人，後徙於陝。

translations.literal: Yu Chongliang, style name Zhongyi, his ancestors were from Shanyang in Chuzhou and later moved to Shan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chongliang, styled Zhongyi, came from a family originally of Shanyang in Chuzhou that later relocated to Shan.

sentences.zh: 崇諒初名崇遠，後避漢祖諱改之。

translations.literal: Chongliang was originally named Chongyuan; later he changed it to avoid the taboo name of the Han founding emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Chongliang had originally been named Chongyuan but changed his name to avoid the imperial taboo of the Han founder.

sentences.zh: 幼能屬文，弱冠，相州刺史辟為從事。

translations.literal: From youth he could compose essays; at capped age the prefect of Xiangzhou recruited him as a staff member.
translations.idiomatic: He could write essays from childhood, and upon reaching adulthood he was recruited as a staff officer by the prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 會魏帥楊師厚卒，建相州為昭德軍，分魏郡州縣之半以隸之。

translations.literal: When the Wei commander Yang Shihou died, Xiangzhou was established as the Zhaode Army, and half of the Wei prefecture's counties were divided to be subordinated to it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei military governor Yang Shihou died, Xiangzhou was made the seat of the Zhaode Army, and half of the counties of Wei Prefecture were placed under its jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 魏人不便，裨校張彥及帳下，囚節度使賀德倫歸款莊宗，崇諒奔歸陝。

translations.literal: The Wei people were displeased; staff officer Zhang Yan and those under the command imprisoned Military Commissioner He Delun and submitted to Zhuangzong; Chongliang fled back to Shan.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wei were unhappy with the change; staff officer Zhang Yan and his followers imprisoned Military Commissioner He Delun and surrendered to Zhuangzong, while Chongliang fled back to Shan.

sentences.zh: 漢祖之入，盡索崇諒所受契丹詔敕，焚於朝堂，復令知製制誥。

translations.literal: When the Han founding emperor entered, he thoroughly searched out the Khitan edicts and orders Chongliang had received, burned them in the court hall, and again ordered him to draft edicts.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han founder took power, he had all the Khitan edicts Chongliang had received seized and burned in the court hall, then restored him to the duty of drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 俄拜翰林學士，就加中書舍人。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Hanlin academician and concurrently made Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Hanlin academician and concurrently made Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 隱帝即位，崇諒以母老求就養，除保義軍節度副使，領台州刺史，食郡奉。

translations.literal: When the Hidden Emperor acceded, Chongliang because his mother was old requested nearby care; he was appointed vice military commissioner of the Baoyi Army, concurrently prefect of Taizhou, receiving prefectural salary.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yin acceded, Chongliang asked to be posted near home to care for his aging mother; he was appointed vice military commissioner of the Baoyi Army with the concurrent title of prefect of Taizhou and drew the prefectural salary.

sentences.zh: 會舉師討三叛，節度使白文珂在軍前，崇諒知後事。

translations.literal: When troops were raised to suppress the three rebellions, Military Commissioner Bai Wenke was at the army front; Chongliang handled rear affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When an expedition was launched against the three rebellions, Military Commissioner Bai Wenke took the field while Chongliang managed affairs behind the lines.

sentences.zh: 凡供軍儲備調發，皆促期而辦，近鎮賴之。

translations.literal: In all matters of supplying army stores and preparing transfers, everything was completed within urgent deadlines; nearby garrison towns relied on this.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever the army needed in stores or transfers, he met every deadline, and the surrounding commands depended on him.

sentences.zh: 崇諒親屬盡在鳳翔城中，逾年城破，李穀為轉運使，庇護崇諒家數十口，皆無恙。

translations.literal: All of Chongliang's relatives were in Fengxiang city; after more than a year the city fell. Li Gu was transport commissioner and sheltered several dozen members of Chongliang's household—all unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: Chongliang's entire family was trapped in Fengxiang; when the city fell after more than a year, Transport Commissioner Li Gu sheltered several dozen of his kin, and none came to harm.

sentences.zh: 崇諒請告，自岐迎居於陝。

translations.literal: Chongliang requested leave; from Qi he welcomed them to settle in Shan.
translations.idiomatic: Chongliang took leave to go from Qi and bring them to live with him in Shan.

sentences.zh: 未幾，王仁裕罷內職，朝議請召崇諒為學士。

translations.literal: Before long Wang Renyu was dismissed from inner-court service; court discussion requested summoning Chongliang as academician.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Wang Renyu left his inner-court post, and the court proposed recalling Chongliang as a Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 周祖踐祚，書詔繁委，皆崇諒為之。

translations.literal: When Zhou's founding emperor ascended the throne, written edicts were numerous and complex—all were done by Chongliang.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhou founder took the throne, the flood of written edicts all passed through Chongliang's hand.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，加工部侍郎，充職。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun he was given the additional title Vice Director of the Ministry of Works while filling his post.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangshun era he was additionally made Vice Director of the Ministry of Works and continued in his duties.

sentences.zh: 會兗州慕容彥超加封邑，彥超已懷反側，遣崇諒充使賜官告，仍慰撫之。

translations.literal: When Yan Prefecture's Murong Yanchao received an enlarged fief, Yanchao already harbored rebellious intent; Chongliang was sent as envoy to bestow the appointment certificate, and also to console and reassure him.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Yanchao of Yanzhou was granted an enlarged fief, he was already nursing treasonous thoughts; Chongliang was dispatched to present the patent of appointment and offer reassuring words.

sentences.zh: 時多進策人，命崇諒就樞密院引試，考定升降。

translations.literal: At the time many policy submitters came forward; he was ordered to conduct preliminary exams at the Bureau of Military Affairs and determine promotion or demotion.
translations.idiomatic: With many men then submitting policy proposals, the court had Chongliang examine candidates at the Bureau of Military Affairs and rank them for promotion or demotion.

sentences.zh: 崇諒以母老思鄉里，求解官歸養。

translations.literal: Chongliang because his mother was old and missed her homeland requested to resign office and return home to support her.
translations.idiomatic: With an aging mother who longed for home, Chongliang asked to leave office and return to care for her.

sentences.zh: 詔給長告，賜其母衣服、繒帛、茶藥、緡錢，假滿百日，令本州月給錢三萬，米麪十五斛。

translations.literal: An edict granted extended leave and bestowed on his mother clothes, silk, tea and medicine, and strings of cash; when the leave period of one hundred days ended, his home prefecture was ordered to give monthly thirty thousand cash and fifteen bushels of rice and flour.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted him extended leave and sent his mother gifts of clothing, silk, tea, medicine, and cash; after the hundred-day leave, his home prefecture was to pay him thirty thousand cash and fifteen bushels of grain each month.

sentences.zh: 俄拜禮部侍郎，復為學士。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites and again made academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites and restored as a Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 詔令侍母歸闕，崇諒再表以母老病乞終養，優詔不允。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to attend his mother and return to court; Chongliang memorialized again that his mother was old and ill and begged lifelong care; a gracious edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When ordered to bring his mother back to court, Chongliang memorialized again citing her age and illness and pleading to retire for good to support her; the emperor's gracious reply refused.

sentences.zh: 世宗征高平，崇諒尚未至，陶穀乘間言曰：「魚崇諒逗留不來，有顧望意。

translations.literal: When Shizong campaigned at Gaoping, Chongliang had not yet arrived; Tao Gu seized an opening and said, "Yu Chongliang lingers and does not come—he has a mind of hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Shizong's Gaoping campaign, Chongliang had not yet reported for duty; Tao Gu seized the moment and said, "Yu Chongliang is dragging his feet and never showing up—he is clearly wavering.

sentences.zh: 」世宗頗疑之。

translations.literal: " Shizong became quite suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor grew quite suspicious of him.

sentences.zh: 崇諒又表陳母病，詔許歸陝州就養。

translations.literal: Chongliang memorialized again stating his mother's illness; an edict permitted him to return to Shan Prefecture for nearby care.
translations.idiomatic: Chongliang submitted another memorial citing his mother's illness, and the emperor allowed him to retire to Shanzhou and care for her there.

sentences.zh: 訖太祖朝不起。

translations.literal: Through the Taizu reign he did not take office again.
translations.idiomatic: He never returned to office for the rest of Emperor Taizu's reign.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，詔授金紫光祿大夫、尚書兵部侍郎致仕。

translations.literal: When Taizong acceded, an edict conferred Golden Purple-Glow Grand Master of the Palace and Vice Director of the Ministry of War in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong acceded, he was granted the titles Golden Purple-Glow Grand Master of the Palace and Vice Director of the Ministry of War in honorific retirement.

sentences.zh: 歲餘卒。

translations.literal: After more than a year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died a little over a year later.

sentences.zh: 張澹，字成文，其先南陽人，徙家河南。

translations.literal: Zhang Dan, style name Chenwen, his ancestors were from Nanyang and moved the family to Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dan, styled Chenwen, came from a family originally of Nanyang that later settled in Henan.

sentences.zh: 澹幼而好學，有才藻。

translations.literal: Dan from youth loved learning and had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Dan loved learning from childhood and showed real literary gift.

sentences.zh: 晉開運初，登進士第。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin's Kaiyun era he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Kaiyun era of Later Jin he earned his jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 宰相桑維翰器之，妻以女。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Sang Weihan valued him and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Sang Weihan took a liking to him and married him to his daughter.

sentences.zh: 解褐校書郎，直昭文館，再遷秘書郎，充鹽鐵推官，歷左拾遺、禮部員外郎，並充史館修撰。

translations.literal: He began his career as proofreader, served in the Zhaowen Hall, was twice promoted to secretary, served as Salt and Iron Commission investigating officer, passed through Left Reminder and Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites, and all concurrently served as historiographer in the History Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a proofreader and staff member of the Zhaowen Hall, rose to secretary, served as an investigating officer on the Salt and Iron Commission, held the posts of Left Reminder and Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites, and throughout also worked as a historiographer in the History Institute.

sentences.zh: 出為洛陽令，秩滿，授吏部員外，復充史館修撰。

translations.literal: He went out as magistrate of Luoyang; when his term ended he was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and again served as History Institute compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Luoyang, and when his term expired he was made Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and again assigned to the History Institute.

sentences.zh: 周恭帝初，拜右司員外郎、知制誥。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhou's Gongdi reign he was appointed Right Division Vice Director and drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the reign of Zhou's Gongdi he was made Right Division Vice Director and put in charge of drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，加祠部郎中。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong he was additionally made Director of the Ministry of Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianlong 2 he was further promoted to Director of the Ministry of Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 會秘書郎張去華上書自薦有文藝，願與澹及祠部員外郎知制誥盧多遜、殿中侍御史師頌並試，覈定優劣。

translations.literal: When Secretary Zhang Quhua submitted a memorial recommending himself for literary talent, wishing to compete together with Dan, Secretariat Director and Edict Drafter Lu Duosun, and Palace Attendant Censor Shi Song in a joint test to determine superiority and inferiority.
translations.idiomatic: Secretary Zhang Quhua then submitted a memorial claiming literary merit and asking to compete alongside Dan, Edict Drafter Lu Duosun of the Ministry of Sacrifices, and Palace Attendant Censor Shi Song so their relative talents could be judged.

sentences.zh: 太祖令並試於講武殿，澹所對不應策問，責授左司員外郎。

translations.literal: Taizu ordered them all tested in the Hall of Martial Lectures; Dan's answers did not fit the policy questions, and he was demoted to Left Division Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu had them examined in the Hall of Martial Lectures; Dan's answers missed the point of the policy questions, and he was demoted to Left Division Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 未幾，通判泰州兼海陵鹽監副使。

translations.literal: Before long he was made co-prefect of Taizhou and concurrently deputy commissioner of the Hailing Salt Monopoly.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was assigned as co-prefect of Taizhou and deputy commissioner of the Hailing salt works.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，通判梓州，復拜祠部郎中。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified he was co-prefect of Zizhou and again appointed Director of the Ministry of Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest of Shu he served as co-prefect of Zizhou and was again made Director of the Ministry of Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 開寶初，就轉倉部郎中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaibao he was transferred in place to Director of the Ministry of Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaibao era he was transferred on the spot to Director of the Ministry of Granaries.

sentences.zh: 四年冬，以本官復知制誥。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, winter, with his current rank he again drafted edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fourth year he resumed drafting edicts at his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 六年，會李昉責授，盧多遜使江南，內署闕學士，太祖令澹權直學士院。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, when Li Fang was demoted and Lu Duosun went on mission to Jiangnan, the inner secretariat lacked an academician; Taizu ordered Dan to serve temporarily as head of duty in the Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, with Li Fang demoted and Lu Duosun dispatched to Jiangnan, the inner secretariat had no academician on duty; Taizu had Dan serve temporarily as head of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 七年長春節，攝殿中監，進酒，命賜金紫。

translations.literal: On the seventh year's Changchun festival he acted as Director of the Palace Receptions, presented wine, and was ordered granted golden-purple insignia.
translations.idiomatic: At the Changchun festival in the seventh year he acted as Director of the Palace Receptions and presented the wine; the emperor then granted him golden-purple insignia.

sentences.zh: 六月，權點檢三司事。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he was given temporary charge of inspecting Three Departments affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he was temporarily put in charge of inspecting Three Departments affairs.

sentences.zh: 不逾旬，疽發背卒，年五十六。

translations.literal: Within ten days a carbuncle broke out on his back and he died, age fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In less than ten days a carbuncle on his back brought him down; he was fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞其無子，甚愍之，命中使護葬於洛陽。

translations.literal: Taizu heard he had no son, was greatly moved, and ordered a palace envoy to oversee burial in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Learning he had no son, Taizu was deeply moved and ordered a palace envoy to supervise his burial in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 澹美風儀，善談論，歷官釐務，所至皆治。

translations.literal: Dan had fine bearing, was skilled at discourse, and in successive offices clarified affairs—wherever he went all was well governed.
translations.idiomatic: Dan had an elegant bearing and a gift for conversation; in every post he took up he put affairs in order and left things well governed.

sentences.zh: 初與詞臣校藝，黜居郎署，頗怏怏。

translations.literal: When first competing in literary skill with drafting officials he was dismissed to bureau posts and was quite resentful.
translations.idiomatic: After losing a literary contest to fellow drafters and being pushed back to routine bureau work, he was deeply discontented.

sentences.zh: 晚年附會盧多遜，方再獲進用。

translations.literal: In his later years he attached himself to Lu Duosun and only then regained advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Only in his later years, by currying favor with Lu Duosun, did he win promotion again.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，太宗論及文士，曰：「澹典書命而試以策，非其所長，此蓋陶穀、高錫黨張去華以沮澹爾。

translations.literal: In the Chunhua era Taizong discussed literary men and said, "Dan was in charge of imperial documents yet was tested by policy questions—not his strength; this was surely Tao Gu and Gao Xi banding with Zhang Quhua to thwart Dan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chunhua era, discussing men of letters, Emperor Taizong said, "Dan had been drafting imperial edicts, yet they tested him on policy questions—not his forte. Surely Tao Gu and Gao Xi rallied behind Zhang Quhua to block Dan's path.

sentences.zh: 若使穀輩出其不意而遽試之，豈有不失律者邪？」

translations.literal: If Gu and his ilk were suddenly tested without warning, would there not be those who failed the standards?"
translations.idiomatic: If Gu and his friends were tested out of the blue, would none of them miss the mark?"

sentences.zh: 高錫，字天福，河中虞鄉人。

translations.literal: Gao Xi, style name Tianfu, was a native of Yuxiang in Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xi, styled Tianfu, came from Yuxiang in Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 家世業儒，幼潁悟，能屬文。

translations.literal: His family for generations pursued Confucian studies; from youth he was quick-witted and could compose essays.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long been devoted to learning; bright from childhood, he could already write essays.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐中，舉進士。

translations.literal: In Han's Qianyou era he was recommended for the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianyou era of Later Han he sat for the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 王晏鎮徐州，辟掌書記；

translations.literal: When Wang Yan commanded Xuzhou he recruited him as chief secretary;
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Yan governed Xuzhou he recruited Xi as his chief secretary;

sentences.zh: 留守西洛，又辟河南府推官。

translations.literal: when stationed at Western Luoyang he again recruited him as investigating officer of Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: and when Wang held the western capital he also appointed Xi investigating officer of Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 坐按獄失實奪官，遷置涇州，會赦得歸。

translations.literal: He was stripped of office for investigating a case that did not accord with facts, was transferred and assigned to Jing Prefecture, and upon a general amnesty was allowed to return.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his post when a criminal case he handled proved unfounded; after being reassigned to Jing Prefecture he was able to return home when an amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 周顯德初，劉崇入寇，宰相請選將拒之，世宗銳意親征，破崇高平，誅敗將樊愛能等，由是政無大小悉親決之，不復責成有司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhou's Xiande era, Liu Chong invaded; the chief minister requested selecting a general to resist him; Shizong was keen to campaign in person, crushed the enemy at Gaoping, executed the defeated generals Fan Aineng and others; from this all affairs great and small he decided in person, no longer charging the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiande era, when Liu Chong raided the border, the chief minister urged sending a general against him; Emperor Shizong insisted on taking the field himself, won at Gaoping, and executed the failed generals Fan Aineng and others. From then on he decided every matter himself, great or small, and no longer held the regular offices accountable.

sentences.zh: 錫徒步詣招諫匭上書，請擇賢任官，分治眾職，疏奏不報。

translations.literal: Xi went on foot to the suggestion and remonstrance box and submitted a memorial requesting selecting the worthy for office and dividing governance of many duties; the memorial received no response.
translations.idiomatic: Xi walked to the public suggestion box and submitted a memorial urging the appointment of worthy men and a proper division of duties among offices; it went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 世宗嘗令翰林學士及兩省官分撰俳優詞，付教坊肄習，以奉遊宴。

translations.literal: Shizong once ordered Hanlin academicians and officials of the two secretariats separately to compose variety-player lyrics, delivered to the Court Entertainment Office for drill, to serve banquets and excursions.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong once ordered Hanlin academicians and Secretariat officials to compose lyrics for variety players, have them rehearsed at the Court Entertainment Office, and perform them at his banquets and outings.

sentences.zh: 錫復上疏諫。

translations.literal: Xi again submitted a memorial remonstrating.
translations.idiomatic: Xi submitted another memorial in protest.

sentences.zh: 後為蔡州防禦推官。

translations.literal: Later he served as investigating officer on the Cai Prefecture defense staff.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as investigating officer on the defense staff of Cai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宋初，棄官歸京師，詣匭上疏，請禁兵器，疏入不報。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he abandoned office and returned to the capital, went to the box and submitted a memorial requesting prohibition of weapons; when the memorial entered court there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he quit his post and returned to the capital, placed another memorial in the suggestion box calling for a ban on private arms, and again received no answer.

sentences.zh: 建隆五年，又以書干宰相范質，質奏用為著作佐郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jianlong he again by letter approached Chief Minister Fan Zhi; Zhi memorialized to employ him as Assistant Archivist.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianlong 5 he wrote to Chief Minister Fan Zhi, who recommended him for the post of Assistant Archivist.

sentences.zh: 明年春，遷監察御史。

translations.literal: The next spring he was promoted to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring he was promoted to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 秋，拜左拾遺、知制誥，加屯田員外郎。

translations.literal: In autumn he was appointed Left Reminder and drafter of edicts, with the additional title Vice Director of the Ministry of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was made Left Reminder and edict drafter, with the additional title of Vice Director of the Ministry of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 乾德初，賜緋。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qiande he was granted crimson robes.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qiande era he was granted the privilege of crimson robes.

sentences.zh: 太宗尹京，石熙載在幕中，錫弟銑應進士舉，干熙載，望首薦。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Zhao governed the capital, Shi Xizai was in his staff; Xi's younger brother Xian sat for the jinshi examination and approached Xizai, hoping for first recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Taizong governed the capital, Shi Xizai served on his staff; Xi's younger brother Xian took the jinshi examination and importuned Xizai, hoping to be ranked first among recommendees.

sentences.zh: 銑辭藝淺薄，熙載不許，錫深銜之，數於帝前言熙載裨讚無狀。

translations.literal: Xian's literary skill was shallow and thin; Xizai did not permit it; Xi deeply harbored resentment and repeatedly before the emperor spoke that Xizai's minor praises were unseemly.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's writing was plainly weak, and Xizai refused; Xi nursed a deep grudge and repeatedly told the emperor that Xizai's fawning praise was shameless.

sentences.zh: 帝具以語太宗，且曰：「當為汝擇人代之。

translations.literal: The emperor fully told this to the Prince of Zhao and also said, "I shall choose someone to replace him for you.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reported all of this to the Prince of Zhao and added, "I will find someone else to replace him for you.

sentences.zh: 」太宗曰：「熙載勤於乃職，聞高錫嘗求薦其弟，熙載拒之，慮為錫所構。

translations.literal: " The Prince of Zhao said, "Xizai is diligent in his duties; I hear Gao Xi once sought recommendation for his younger brother and Xizai refused—I fear he is being framed by Xi.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince replied, "Xizai has been diligent in his post. I hear Gao Xi once tried to get his brother recommended and Xizai turned him down—I worry he is being set up by Xi.

sentences.zh: 」帝大悟，雖怒之，未有以發。

translations.literal: " The emperor greatly understood; though angry, he had no means to act.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor saw the truth at once. Though he was furious with Xi, he had no immediate grounds to move against him.

sentences.zh: 會使青州，私受節帥郭崇賂遺；

translations.literal: When on mission to Qing Prefecture he privately received bribes and gifts from Military Commissioner Guo Chong;
translations.idiomatic: When sent on a mission to Qingzhou he secretly accepted gifts from Military Commissioner Guo Chong;

sentences.zh: 又嘗致書澧州刺史為僧求紫衣，為人所告。

translations.literal: he also once sent a letter to the prefect of Li Prefecture seeking purple robes for a monk, and was reported by someone.
translations.idiomatic: he also once wrote the prefect of Lizhou on behalf of a monk seeking purple robes, and someone denounced him.

sentences.zh: 事下御史府核實，責貶萊州司馬。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to the censorate for verification; he was demoted to military adjutant of Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate investigated and confirmed the charges, and he was demoted to military adjutant of Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 遇赦，改均州別駕，移陳州。

translations.literal: Upon general amnesty he was changed to Vice Prefect of Jun Prefecture and transferred to Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After a general amnesty he was reassigned as vice prefect of Junzhou and later transferred to Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 太平興國八年，卒。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taiping Xingguo he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth year of the Taiping Xingguo era.

sentences.zh: 兄子冕。

translations.literal: His elder brother's son Mián.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Mián.

sentences.zh: 從子 冕

translations.literal: Nephew Mián.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Mián.

sentences.zh: 冕，字子莊，周顯德中，詣闕上書，稱旨，擢為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Mián, style name Zizhuang—in Zhou's Xiande era he went to court and submitted a memorial; it accorded with the emperor's intent, and he was elevated to Remonstrance and Advice Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: Mián, styled Zizhuang, went to court during the Xiande era with a memorial that pleased the emperor, and was raised straight to Remonstrance and Advice Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 宰相范質以為超擢太過，詔特授將仕郎，守右補闕，賜賚加等。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Fan Zhi considered the leap in promotion excessive; an edict specially appointed him Entry-Level Gentleman, acting Right Supplementation Reminder, with increased bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Fan Zhi thought the promotion too steep; the emperor instead made him an Entry-Level Gentleman acting as Right Supplementation Reminder, with extra gifts.

sentences.zh: 宋初，由膳部都官員外郎累至膳部郎中，出知益州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, from Vice Director of the Ministries of Food and Justice he rose cumulatively to Director of the Ministry of Food; he went out as prefect of Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he rose from vice director of the ministries of food and justice to director of the ministry of food, then was sent out to govern Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，卒，年五十。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi he died, age fifty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yongxi 2 at the age of fifty.

sentences.zh: 贈右諫議大夫，錄其子垂休為固始主簿。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Right Remonstrance and Advice Grand Master; his son Chuixiu was recorded as magistrate of Gushi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given the title Right Remonstrance and Advice Grand Master, and his son Chuixiu was enrolled as magistrate of Gushi.

sentences.zh: 論曰：自唐以來，翰林直學士與中書舍人對掌訓辭，頌宣功德，箴諫闕失，不專為文墨之職也。

translations.literal: Discussion says: From Tang onward, Hanlin academicians on duty and Secretariat drafters jointly held charge of imperial instruction, praising and proclaiming merit and virtue, admonishing and remonstrating over omissions and faults—they were not posts devoted solely to brush and ink.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Since Tang times, Hanlin academicians on duty and Secretariat drafters had jointly handled imperial pronouncements—celebrating merit, proclaiming virtue, and rebuking failings. These were not posts confined to literary ornament alone.

sentences.zh: 宋興，亦采詞藻以備斯選，若穀之才雋，著之敏達，澹之治跡，錫之策慮，冕之敦質，咸有可觀。

translations.literal: When Song arose it likewise drew on literary ornament to fill these selections; as for Gu's keen talent, Zhe's quick clarity, Dan's record of good governance, Xi's policy deliberations, Mián's solid sincerity—all had points worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Song as well, literary talent was still sought for these posts; Gu's sharp brilliance, Zhe's quick mind, Dan's administrative record, Xi's policy counsel, and Mián's steady character all had something to commend them.

sentences.zh: 然豫成禪代之詔，見薄時君，終身不獲大用。

translations.literal: Yet those who beforehand completed the abdication-transfer edict were held in slight esteem by the rulers of the age and throughout life did not receive great employment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those who had drafted the edicts facilitating the dynastic transition were viewed coldly by their emperors and never won high trust again.

sentences.zh: 及夫險詖忌前，酣醟少檢，附勢希榮，構讒謀己，皆無取焉。

translations.literal: As for those who were treacherous and jealous of predecessors, drunk and unrestrained with little self-restraint, attached to power hoping for glory, framed slander to scheme for themselves—all are unworthy of esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Treachery and jealousy of one's betters, dissipation without restraint, clinging to power for advancement, and weaving slander for personal gain—all of this deserves no respect.

sentences.zh: 蒙博洽長厚，繼竇儀裁定儀制，惜乎南郊之議，請去太祖以宣祖配天，為識者所非。

translations.literal: Meng was broadly learned and generous and long-suffering; he succeeded Dou Yi in fixing ritual regulations—alas, in the discussion of the Southern Suburban Sacrifice he requested removing Taizu and pairing Xu ancestor with Heaven, and was faulted by the knowing.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Meng was learned, generous, and long-suffering; after Dou Yi he helped set the court's ritual code. Yet in the debate over the southern suburban sacrifice he urged replacing Emperor Taizu with Emperor Xuan as Heaven's consort—a proposal wise men rejected.

sentences.zh: 昭儉抗論跋扈，志除驕將，而多言歷詆，自取惡名，抑好訐為直者與？

translations.literal: Zhaojian boldly argued against overbearing arrogance, his aim to remove proud generals—yet with many words he repeatedly slandered and earned himself an ill name; was he perhaps one who loves exposing faults as uprightness?
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhaojian spoke boldly against arrogant power and meant to bring down overbearing generals, but his ceaseless invective earned him a foul reputation. Was he, perhaps, one of those who mistake hostility for honesty?

sentences.zh: 崇諒奉親篤至，反罹間毀，終身歸養，而不復起，後蒙旌賁之典，則為善者聳動矣。

translations.literal: Chongliang in serving his kin was utterly devoted, yet on the contrary suffered slander amid the damage; he spent life in return-care and did not rise again—later he received the classic of commendation and ornament, and then those who do good were stirred and moved.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chongliang was utterly devoted to his mother, yet was slandered for his trouble, retired for good to care for her, and never served again. When the court later honored him posthumously, it heartened every man who would do right.

sentences.zh: 祜以百口明符彥卿無他志，且言以猜忌殺無辜者享國不長，因以杜太宗之他疑，又卻盧多遜之傾趙普，以致被黜，仁者有後，宜乎子旦為宋元臣焉。

translations.literal: You with a hundred mouths clarified that Fu Yanqing had no other intent, and moreover said that killing the innocent through suspicion makes a state not long enjoyed—thereby blocking the Prince of Zhao's other suspicions; he also turned back Lu Duosun's overthrow of Zhao Pu, thereby meeting demotion; the benevolent have descendants—fitting indeed that his son Dan became a great Song minister.
translations.idiomatic: Wang You staked his family's lives on vouching that Fu Yanqing had no treasonous intent and warned that rulers who slaughter the innocent out of suspicion do not long keep the throne—thereby easing the future Emperor Taizong's doubts. He also blocked Lu Duosun's move against Zhao Pu and was demoted for it. The virtuous are rewarded in their heirs; little wonder that his son Dan became one of the great ministers of the Song.
